1	# Release execution
2	
3	The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).
4	
5	## Terms
6	
7	- Package: a dependency-graph node owned by a directory; it can expose several canonical manifest/distribution identities.
8	- Distribution identity: `ReleasePackageId`, an ecosystem-qualified native package name. A graph package with several identities has one tag, one forge release and one forge publish, each carried by the package's owner: its first selected identity in manifest order (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI).
9	- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto does not parse `target`; CI supplies product-slot bytes and Callisto records where they go. Registry publishing can invoke native build/pack tools, including Python's build backend.
10	- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
11	- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
12	- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
13	- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish.
14	
15	## Layers
16	
17	| Layer | Crate | Contents |
18	| --- | --- | --- |
19	| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release/execution.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
20	| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
21	| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release build-python`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |
22	
23	## Two routes, one executor
24	
25	```
26	local:  derive_release_roster (untagged versions, plus tagged-on-HEAD releases not fully observed)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
27	CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
28	both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
29	```
30	
31	- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
32	- A tag proves only that the tag was created. `incomplete_tagged_releases` observes every operation of the packages tagged on HEAD and keeps any not exactly satisfied; a tag on another commit is never observed.
33	- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
34	- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.
35	
36	## Managed release PR and workflow
37	
38	Callisto's own [release workflow](../../.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml) reconstructs one `callisto/version-packages` PR from `main` when changesets land. It versions manifests and changelogs; merging the PR consumes the changesets on `main` and authorizes publication.
39	
40	- The action commits non-workflow changes through `createCommitOnBranch`, then moves the release ref through REST. It does not run a local `git push`. Workflow files remain unchanged, so the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs no workflow-write permission.
41	- Commits are GitHub-signed as `github-actions[bot]`. An App or fine-grained token can use another identity.
42	- Branch protection must require reviews and CI checks. CODEOWNERS alone does not enforce review.
43	- `version-pr` maintains the PR; `release` runs the local release route. Artifact and platform packages use plan/build/execute. Deprecated `publish` and `create_github_release` action inputs are ignored. The [action manifest](../../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml) defines current inputs and outputs.
44	- Only `execute` receives registry credentials. Plan and build jobs receive none. Temporary intent, receipt, artifacts, and build output live under `RUNNER_TEMP`, outside the checkout.
45	
46	GitHub Actions schedules jobs, transports artifacts, and injects credentials. Callisto validates source, provenance, plan, observations, transitions, terminality, receipts, and artifacts. Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics. Recovery dispatch uses current orchestration on `main` with an explicit merged source SHA and runs credential-free `recovery-checks` instead of full `verify`.
47	
48	The generated release action maps credentials without changing owner-defined publish hooks:
49	
50	- npm: copy existing user config to a mode-0600 temporary file, add an npmjs entry interpolating `NPM_TOKEN`, point npm-compatible tools at it, and remove it on exit. The original config is unchanged. `NPM_TOKEN` remains available for native hooks and `.npmrc` interpolation. Custom registries use native configuration.
51	- Bun: also set `NPM_CONFIG_TOKEN`, because Bun does not honor `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`.
52	- PyPI: map `PYPI_TOKEN` to `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__` and `TWINE_PASSWORD` for upload. The build backend receives no registry or forge credentials.
53	- Cargo: pass `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` through to Cargo.
54	
55	## Run envelope and state (`release/execution.rs`)
56	
57	- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
58	- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
59	- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
60	- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
61	- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.
62	
63	## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)
64	
65	- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
66	- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
67	- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
68	- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
69	- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.
70	
71	Provider reads use native tools for Cargo and npm, and `curl` for PyPI's PEP 691 JSON simple index:
72	
73	- Cargo: `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY` runs from the source root. Matching `version:` means exact; exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` means absent. Other results are indeterminate. Yanked versions are invisible to `cargo info`; a rejected publish ends without a receipt.
74	- npm: `npm view NAME@VERSION version --json`.
75	- PyPI: a matching file means exact; 404 or no match means absent; transport failure or non-JSON means indeterminate. Yanked matches count as absent. Before an effect, `release execute` also builds the release's files once into a temporary directory and compares their names with the index, so a partly uploaded release uploads only what is missing and is satisfied only when the whole set is there.
76	
77	These reads are version-level checks, not proof of identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. Registry endpoints must be HTTPS. Read-only observations retry 429, 5xx, rate-limited 403, and transport failures with backoff and `Retry-After`. Effects are never blindly retried; outbound commands have deadlines.
78	
79	## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)
80	
81	`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:
82	
83	| From | Event | To |
84	| --- | --- | --- |
85	| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
86	| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
87	| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
88	| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
89	| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |
90	
91	- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
92	- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
93	- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).
94	
95	## Forge ordering
96	
97	- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
98	- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup finds the release ID by tag through GraphQL, then reads the release by ID (`release/github.rs`).
99	- GitHub's reads lag its writes by seconds. The check right after this run's own create, upload or publish retries an absent answer for about a minute before it reports a conflict (`observe_until_visible`).
100	
101	The tag/announcement barrier covers all required publications of a graph package: a package's tag waits for the registry publishes of every release identity it has (`OpIndex::tag_prerequisites`), so a dual Cargo/npm owner's one tag and public release follow both publishes, in no fixed ecosystem order. Selecting one identity of a dual package makes that identity the owner, so the tag waits only for the selected publishes. An intent derived before this rule fails closed as stale and is rebuilt with `release plan`. See [the scoped design](polyglot-v1.md) for proposed ownership and future Go tag-publication semantics.
102	
103	## Wire and observation boundaries
104	
105	Stdout JSON reports include `schemaVersion`, `command` and `dryRun`; durable decision, intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files retain their own wire shapes. The CLI's `release-pr verify` reader accepts both the strict bare decision and unchanged decide report, validating the report metadata before passing the payload to the shared domain constructor. Unknown and duplicate fields remain errors; durable wire readers are unchanged. The real-binary action contract exercises this producer/consumer boundary through inline, file and stdin inputs.
106	
107	Managed PR verification compares the original snapshot before staging and before moving the release ref. After a successful update, the action confirms the ref's exact new SHA and supplies it as `--applied-head` for the final check. The model validates the original update decision and allows only its selected PR's head to change to that SHA; the base, repository, PR roster and every other head remain unchanged. Create decisions keep strict equality until the PR is created. The action does not rewrite its decision or discard concurrency checks after its own effect.
108	
109	Registry evidence currently confirms a version, with optional checksum/yank fields; it does not establish byte identity. Python completion has two modes. Without a sealed file set (the local route, and a CI route whose manifest seals none) it is judged against the files the executing run builds, matched by name, and digests are compared only for files that run uploaded: a rebuild need not be byte-identical to an earlier attempt. With a sealed set, a build job (`release build-python`, no credentials) builds the files and `release artifact-manifest --seal-python` records each file's name, size and sha256 in the manifest, so the envelope's manifest digest covers them. `release execute` verifies the bytes, builds nothing, uploads those files, and treats any index file under a sealed name with another sha256 as an error (E307). The sealed sets are all or none per plan and each belongs to a Python publish of the intent; the manifest stays at schema version 1 because a manifest without sets is unchanged and an older reader rejects the new field. Artifact size/sha256 validation otherwise applies to declared GitHub assets. Separate private-index read/upload routes are planned, not a shipped guarantee.
110	
111	## Verification tiers
112	
113	- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns.
114	- Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`.
115	- Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`.
116	
117	## Installer and product assets
118	
119	`setup-callisto` defaults to `source: auto`: install the requested release, even in a Callisto checkout. An explicit `version` wins; otherwise `latest` resolves the pinned action ref to its `callisto@` release when possible. A `callisto-cli` manifest alone does not select checkout source.
120	
121	`source: local` builds the checkout and ignores `version`. It requires tracked root and CLI manifests, the CLI entrypoint, a Cargo-confirmed workspace member and binary target, Git, Cargo, jq, and locked offline metadata resolution. It uses the checkout's `target/` cache, installs under `RUNNER_TEMP`, and never falls back from invalid local source. Callisto's release jobs use this mode.
122	
123	Downloaded binaries are checked with `gh attestation verify` against `orin-dx/callisto` and the `callisto-release.yml` signer before extraction. Only the `callisto` binary is extracted. `verification: require` aborts on failure; `fallback` (default) deletes the asset and installs from crates.io; `skip` warns and uses it. Fallback pins the requested version except for `latest`. Older unattested releases motivate the default. `require` and `fallback` never run an unverified asset.
124	
125	Product assets target `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`. Apple signing and notarization are out of scope. GitHub provenance binds assets to the orchestration revision; the intent and artifact manifest bind their bytes to the release source. Callisto publishes its crates to crates.io and product assets to GitHub Releases, not to another registry for rehearsal.
126

1	# 3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state
2	
3	Status: Accepted (implemented in #124)
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	- A release is many external effects (registry publishes, tags, GitHub releases, asset uploads). Any run can die partway.
8	- Owner requirements: a merged but unpublished version must be recoverable without inventing a newer version; execution must fail unless every required operation reaches a verified terminal-success state; partial publication must be safely resumable from provider state (incident report §2, requirements 4, 7, 8).
9	- The same report proposed durably persisted execution state (§8, SPEC-RELEASE-EXECUTION-TERMINALITY criterion 3).
10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	Every run observes each operation's provider state immediately before that operation's effect and adopts an effect that already landed exactly as planned (a registry version already published is adopted with a warning); anything other than exact or absent stops the run (`execute_release`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_execution.rs`). Execution state lives in memory for one run. A receipt is written only when every planned operation reached verified success; an incomplete run exits non-zero. An older merged release is recovered by a fresh run that plans it with `release plan --from-release-commit <sha> --decision <path> --orchestration-revision <current sha>`, not from a state file. Callisto's own release workflow exposes this as a `release_source_sha` dispatch input; workflows generated by `callisto init` do not (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs` tests).
14	
15	## Options considered
16	
17	- **Persisted execution state file with resume** — shipped in #39, proposed again in incident report §8, removed in #124: "CI never reads execution state back (every run is a fresh runner), yet an Initial run turned an already-published registry version into E174, so 'Re-run failed jobs' could never finish a partial release" (#124).
18	- **Recovery commands (`release reconcile`, `release execute --recovery`, `--state`) and Initial/Recovery run kinds** — rejected with the state file in #124. Removed with them: the workspace lock, `AdoptedExact`/`RecoveredExact`, E173, E174 and the release-state schema.
19	- **Rerun the historical workflow run to recover** — rejected. A rerun of an old GitHub Actions run does not pick up workflow fixes merged later (incident report §2 requirement 6; §6 F-003).
20	- **Post-publish re-observation pass to build the receipt** — rejected: a flaky registry read could fail a release whose effects had all landed (#122, #124).
21	
22	## Consequences
23	
24	- A rerun ("Re-run failed jobs" or a fresh run on the release commit) finishes a partial release whose remaining operations can now succeed; "Re-run failed jobs" does not pick up workflow fixes merged later.
25	- Adoption depends on precise observation. An effect that landed differently (for example a conflicting existing tag) must fail closed, never be adopted.
26	- No local record of a failed run survives it; the providers are the record.
27	- Tag identity follows [ADR 9](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md). Python version observation does not establish complete file-set publication; this is tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
28	
29	## Enforcement
30	
31	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_hardening_tests.rs`: `p01_rerun_after_a_failed_publish_publishes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p02_rerun_after_a_crate_is_already_published_completes_and_issues_a_receipt`, `p14_rerun_with_a_conflicting_existing_tag_fails_closed`.
32	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_command_e2e_tests.rs`: `a_failed_run_writes_no_receipt_and_a_rerun_completes`.
33	- `crates/callisto-cli/tests/durable_release_e2e_tests.rs`: `newer_coordinator_executes_and_reruns_an_older_release_source`; rerun scenarios in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_simulator.rs`.
34	- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1` (`crates/callisto-model/src/release/execution.rs`) has no wire shape.
35	
36	## Revisit when
37	
38	- Release execution moves to an environment that keeps state between runs, and a provider cannot be observed well enough to adopt its effects.
39	- A provider offers no reliable way to tell "already landed as planned" from "landed differently".
40	
41	## Sources
42	
43	- PR #124 (592396564), commit bodies and PR body; closed PR #122
44	- PR #101 (279e32361): "reject incomplete quiescent execution", "accept an explicit recovery source"
45	- PR #39 (eeda4a2f5): durable attested execution
46	- Incident report §2, §6 (F-003), §8 (`git show 11038b11b^:.claude/plans/RELEASE-SELF-HOSTING-INCIDENT-2026-09-16.md`)
47

1	# 2. The committed version decision is the release authority
2	
3	Status: Accepted (implemented in #54)
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	- After the release PR merges, CI must verify the merged release commit before any publish, tag or GitHub release runs (PR #54).
8	- Before #54 the release roster was derived from the merged commit's raw diff and understood only a direct changeset-to-package match. It rejected any release in which a `[[fixed-group]]` cascade bumped a sibling that no changeset named (PR #54; code comment on `derive_release_commit_decision`).
9	
10	## Decision
11	
12	`callisto version --emit-decision <path>` writes the version decision it computed (package, target version, inclusion reasons) to `<path>`. The managed release-PR action writes it to `.callisto/release-decision.json` by default (`decision_path` input) and commits it in the release PR. After merge, `release plan --from-release-commit --decision <file>` reads that decision and confirms the merged commit's diff matches it exactly, no more and no less. CI never recomputes changeset, group or cascade policy at that boundary. The verified merge is also the authorization: the release workflow has no separate approval gate (no GitHub Environment approval or required reviewers) (incident report §2, requirements 1 and 2; PR #101, "fix(release): remove Environment approval gate").
13	
14	## Options considered
15	
16	- **Re-derive cascade and group policy in CI after merge, or keep the raw-diff roster and teach it about groups** — rejected. "Rather than teach the re-derivation about groups -- a second, incomplete reimplementation of changeset/group/cascade resolution -- this trusts the decision `callisto version` already computed and committed … One decision surface instead of two that can drift apart" (PR #54).
17	
18	## Consequences
19	
20	- The released roster and versions are exactly those committed in the release PR.
21	- The decision file is a wire contract. Its schema is versioned: `ReleaseDecisionV1::SCHEMA_VERSION` is 2, and the reader accepts 1 and 2 so an older release PR still plans (commit 7027bbfb0).
22	- A decision whose entries do not match its own digest fails to decode (E166) before the diff cross-check. The digest is an unkeyed SHA-256, not a signature, so an edit with a recomputed digest that still passes the decoder's roster checks is caught only by the diff cross-check.
23	- A release commit that does not add or modify the decision file, consumes no changeset, whose manifest versions disagree with the decision, or that leaves a claimed package's changelog untouched is refused (E165). Nothing checks that the decision file was produced by `callisto version --emit-decision`.

# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec: it lists unshipped defects and evidence gaps only. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. No hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run has been performed.

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
| SYS-PYROUTES | `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload. Source-confirmed single-route assumption; servers with distinct read/upload routes cannot generally use one override. Public defaults use separate native routes. | T09-ROUTES | REL-PUB-04/08; private-index policy |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes or the desired npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index; the generated build-matrix workflow seals the file set in a credential-free build job and compares digests, while Python-only workspaces stay unsealed (T09). Universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

## `[registries]`

Keyed by registry name. Two entries exist by default even with no `[registries]` table at all: `crates-io` (kind `cargo`) and `npm` (kind `npm`), both with no URL override.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registries.<name>.kind` | string (`"cargo"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"`) | `"npm"` if omitted | Registry ecosystem |
| `registries.<name>.url` | string | none | Registry endpoint override |

An explicit registry entry still defaults `kind` to npm when omitted; requiring it is planned. Python's URL override currently serves both observation and upload, despite those being separate native APIs; see [Python support limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits). Accepting `nuget` as a target string does not provide a working NuGet publisher.

Example:
```toml
[registries.internal-npm]
kind = "npm"
url = "https://npm.internal.example.com"
```

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact `PackageId` (first matching rule wins, prefixed forms like `cargo/foo` take priority over bare `foo` regardless of declaration order). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is a glob `PackagePattern` and can match many packages at once; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact ecosystem-qualified id or bare name. `[[package-set]]`: glob pattern. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

A package whose wheel name depends on the platform uploads another wheel when rerun on a different machine. A file this run uploads must match the digest the index serves for it; an index that serves no digest is accepted, because only sealed files require one. Builds set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time, which makes hatchling, poetry-core, uv_build and pdm-backend wheels, and setuptools wheels, repeat byte for byte; sdists from setuptools and pdm-backend still differ.
99:- A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).

input.content:
A `pypi` registry read its simple index and uploaded through one URL, so an index whose upload route differs from its read route (Test PyPI's `/simple/` and `/legacy/`) could not be configured.

- `[registries.<name>] publish-url` sets the endpoint Twine uploads to. `url` stays the index Callisto reads, and is also the upload endpoint when `publish-url` is absent, so existing configs behave as before.
- Both endpoints enter the registry binding digest. Changing either makes an earlier intent stale. A binding with no `publish-url` keeps its digest (the pinned intent snapshots only gain the new `publish_endpoint: None` line).
- A package-level `publish-to` index names both routes and ignores the entry's `publish-url`.
- Both URLs follow the same HTTPS, no-userinfo, no-query rules (E126). `publish-url` on a non-`pypi` registry is rejected when the config loads.
- Authenticated reads and HTML-only indexes stay unsupported, and the docs say so.

`RegistryConfig` is public and gains a `publish_url` field, so this is a source-breaking addition for anyone constructing it; `cargo semver-checks` is not part of `just ci`.

Verified: `just ci` passes (coverage 92.7%). The two new provider tests fail when the upload is pointed back at the index. New tests cover the digest staying fixed without `publish-url`, changing with either endpoint, the explicit-index override, unsafe upload URLs, and the config rule. Not exercised against a real private index: the HTTPS-only rule rules out the loopback registry the existing real-tool tests use.

# For each local branch whose PR merged: is the local tip contained in the PR's final head? Is its worktree clean?

OUT=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad

  tip=$(/usr/bin/git rev-parse "refs/heads/$br")
  oid=$(gh pr view "$num" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid 2>/dev/null)
  state=UNSAFE
  if [ "$tip" = "$oid" ]; then
    state=SAME
  else
    /usr/bin/git fetch -q origin "pull/$num/head" 2>/dev/null
    if /usr/bin/git merge-base --is-ancestor "$tip" "$oid" 2>/dev/null; then state=ANCESTOR; fi
  fi
  dirty=n/a
  if [ "$wt" != "none" ] && [ -d "$wt" ]; then
    dirty=$(/usr/bin/git -C "$wt" status --short | grep -v '^??' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    untr=$(/usr/bin/git -C "$wt" status --short | grep '^??' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    dirty="tracked=$dirty untracked=$untr"
  fi
  echo "$state | $br | #$num | wt=$wt | $dirty"

# Road to v1

Unshipped work only. Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). [Owner requirement](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [implementation and stacked-PR execution](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [scoped model and prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

## Scope and guardrails

- Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now, including concrete napi-rs and Cargo/Maturin layouts. Go and C#/.NET/NuGet are architecture examples only.
- Canonical native distribution references; deliberate legacy migration; separate release ownership and version authority.
- Reuse the dependency graph and operation DAG. Native dependency, build input and version coupling do not mean the same thing.
- Native tools/CI own building, packing and authentication. No universal package manager, build scheduler, public plugin platform, service graph or cross-registry transaction.
- Keep committed release authority and provider-observed recovery with no execution journal. Only execute receives registry secrets; no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate in this repo.
- Each implementation PR updates affected specs, tests and docs, with one changeset per independent user-facing topic. Future behavior is not inserted into current specs before its implementation.

## Sequence

The execution portfolio holds the remaining work as bounded units, including the D01 owner-contract checkpoint. The execution guide defines plugin routing, agent write ownership, serial Cargo verification and main-targeted stacked PRs under the existing CI trigger.

### 1. Correct the model in bounded changes

- D01: confirm exact ownership, compatibility, native authority and registry-output proof contracts before architectural code; existing-contract repairs do not wait for it.
- T06 and T06-HISTORY: canonical new references and legacy/history migration across selectors, config, groups, changesets, reports, pre-state and tags. Rename, manifest additions, promotion and demotion retain the right owner's history. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) remains proposed until implementation.
- T07: supported version authority and native distribution representations. Cover co-located Cargo/Maturin with Cargo-owned dynamic Python version and inspect built metadata; do not insert a second static version or build a universal converter.
- T08: shared physical effect ownership, so one tag, draft, upload or publication referenced by several distributions is executed once. The tag already waits for every registry publish of its package, and a rerun after a failed push completes the release. Retain the committed roster and no-journal executor. A future Go source tag is publication, not a universal completion marker.

The plan is an implementation portfolio, not an approved future-behavior spec. Resolve wire/compatibility choices and update the matching area spec with implementation; do not treat architectural packets as fully gated implementer handoffs before D01.

### 2. Reconcile generated workflows

The generated build-matrix workflow builds and places napi addons only for packages in the release intent. Native lifecycle hooks remain package-owner-defined and outside Callisto's release-operation graph; Callisto does not inspect or alter them.

A native Python argv test does not imply a generated Maturin workflow, authenticated private-index observation or complete wheel-set recovery.

### 3. Verify supported workflows and onboarding

Each implementation unit adds its own regression/fault tests. T12 integrates these representative cases through production/native paths; T12-DX measures onboarding:

| Fixture | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo workspace | Inherited/root versions, renamed dependencies, locked resolution and index propagation |
| npm/pnpm | Workspace ranges, aliases, paths, catalogs, peer/optional/private policy and packed metadata |
| Python | Native versions, extras/markers, prereleases, required wheel/sdist set and partial upload |
| Cargo+napi | Selected target builds, owner-defined lifecycle hooks preserved, Callisto-owned publication ordering and clean install/load |
| Cargo+Maturin | Co-located static/dynamic metadata, native version mapping and wheel metadata |
| Mixed workspace | No unrelated addon builds, foreign-name rewrites or missed affected lockfiles |
| History/retry | Correct ownership through transitions; missing push/forge/assets/files completed with original artifacts |

Retain local real-registry tests and record missing prerequisites as skips. Run `just ci` for implementation handoffs and workflow contract/policy checks for workflow changes. Measure fresh-repo first publication against the owner's ten-minute goal. Go/NuGet examples check model assumptions only; they are not new runtime gates.

## Owner decisions

- Canonical-reference compatibility, including colon form; source-owner representation and versioned wire migration.
- Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only scope, npm channel policy, universal checksum requirements and wrapper bump severity.
- Inferred-only/manual releases: managed PR selection depends on changesets and verification requires a consumed changeset (ADR 2). Decide before broadening authorization.
- Build or drop a workspace-wide source-error-discard check; the Cargo lint is only a partial guard.
- Default tags for fixed/independent mode must be settled with canonical ownership, not a second tag-selection mechanism.
- Release-commit provenance: an unkeyed digest and decision/diff agreement do not prove which producer created the file. Decide whether existing authority is sufficient.
- Rust-cache pin in orin-dx/actions, bot-PR check policy and token rotation remain owner items.

## Other open work retained

- Audit literal-false ApplyPermit construction in release/init; enforce dry-run safety at entry boundaries.
- npm writes normalize arbitrary JSON layout; decide whether more than key order/indentation/line endings is needed.
- Preserve redacted stderr for indeterminate provider failures; never stream unredacted native-tool output.
- Publish final migration notices for retired callisto-format, callisto-vcs, callisto-conventional and callisto-changelog, naming callisto-model or callisto-graph.
- Evaluate rustc-provided target facts instead of the 18-triple table without making the core model Rust-target-specific.
- Require kind in explicit registry entries and attest napi .node outputs; define scope before adding a gate.
- Pin the floating moon minor in .prototools after checking proto compatibility.

## After 1.0 (additive)

- Effective-config explain from ConfigProvenance; remove redundant default-valued config afterward.
- .sha256 release-asset sidecars and proto verification.
- Glob fixed-group members.

1	# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership
2	
3	Status: Proposed
4	
5	This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. Evidence and implementation work are recorded in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
10	
11	## Proposed decision
12	
13	- Use canonical slash-qualified distribution references for new exact inputs, authored and generated data; reject new bare and colon-form aliases. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
14	- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
15	- Read existing bare/colon references only through a deliberate compatibility/migration boundary with established ownership. Preserve historical tag ownership without using display promotion as a release-identity change.
16	- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
17	- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
18	- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
19	- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
20	
21	The exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve those unspecified details or introduce release gates.
22	
23	## Options considered
24	
25	- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
26	- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
27	- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.
28	
29	## Consequences
30	
31	Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.
32	
33	## Sources
34	
35	- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
36	- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
37	- [System findings and verification limits](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
38

1	# Scoped polyglot release model
2	
3	Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).
4	
5	## Four concepts
6	
7	| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
8	| --- | --- | --- |
9	| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
10	| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
11	| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
12	| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |
13	
14	Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release-owner representation and wire migration must be specified before implementation.
15	
16	## Canonical references and migration
17	
18	- New exact inputs, generated config, changesets and machine reports use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; new bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names.
19	- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
20	- Existing bare/colon references are migration inputs only, not alternate spellings for new identities. Resolve them only through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Specify historical-reader and schema-version support before changing persisted formats.
21	- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
22	- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags merely to canonicalize selectors.
23	
24	## Native versions and dependencies
25	
26	A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. The initial supported derived-version case is Maturin's Cargo-owned Python version. Preserve `dynamic = ["version"]`, use the known SemVer-to-PEP-440 mapping and verify the built metadata. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter; unsupported mappings and arbitrary SCM-derived backends need an explicit support decision.
27	
28	Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.
29	
30	- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
31	- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
32	- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
33	- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.
34	
35	For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.
36	
37	## Effects and completion
38	
39	For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.
40	
41	Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.
42	
43	A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.
44	
45	PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.
46	
47	Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.
48	
49	## Future compatibility examples
50	
51	- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
52	- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
53	- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.
54	
55	These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.
56	
57	## Prior art and research limits
58	
59	| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
60	| --- | --- | --- |
61	| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
62	| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
63	| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
64	| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |
65	
66	Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).
67	
68	Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
69	
70	## Non-goals
71	
72	No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.

50	## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure
51	
52	Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.
53	
54	- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from the dirty shared checkout.
55	- Current CI triggers only for PRs targeting `main` in `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml`. Default: open cumulative child branches against `main`, label the dependency in the description, and include the parent-only review range. Retargeting to a parent branch would skip this CI; do not do that without a separately approved CI-trigger change.
56	- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
57	- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
58	- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
59	- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
60	- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.

1	# 11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history
2	
3	Status: Accepted (implemented in #167)
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	- A package's id was its primary manifest name. When a second directory declared the same name in another ecosystem, walking promoted both to `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`).
8	- Everything derived from the id changed with it. The default tag template was `{id}@{version}`, so an existing Cargo `foo` looked for `cargo/foo@*` tags, lost `foo@1.0.0`, and planned its next release from no prior tag.
9	- Selectors already tolerate promotion: `cargo/foo` resolves whether or not the package is promoted.
10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	- A package's stable identity is its workspace-relative directory: `Package::key() -> Option<PackageKey>` in `crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs`.
14	- `PackageId` is the display and selector form. Promotion changes how it prints (`foo` becomes `cargo/foo`), which bare selectors are ambiguous (E103), and the namespace of newly created default tags. The directory key and CHANGELOG path do not change.
15	- History recorded under a bare name follows the package that owned the name. Default tags are `{display id}@{version}` (`foo@1.0.0`, then `cargo/foo@1.1.0` once promoted), and a promoted package also finds `foo@*` tags whose commit contains its own manifest and no same-named package's. A bare `pre.json` key moves to the one same-named package that existed when `pre.json` was added. The CHANGELOG path comes from the directory.
16	- No configuration is needed. E101 is raised only when an explicit `tag-template` equals another package's default; E245 only when a bare `pre.json` key has no single owner.
17	
18	## Options considered
19	
20	- **Primary manifest name as key** — rejected: promotion changed the id, and with it the tag lookup of an already-released package.
21	- **Re-key every in-run map by `PackageKey`** — rejected for now: about 66 maps over roughly 1,000 `PackageId` uses. Promotion is computed once per walk, so within a run `PackageId` maps one-to-one onto `PackageKey`; re-keying would change no behavior.
22	- **Default tags from the native name (`foo@{version}`) for every package** — rejected: promoted `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` would share tags, so one of them needed a `tag-template` (E101), and already-promoted workspaces would change their tag names.
23	- **Fall back to `{name}@` tags without an ownership check** — rejected: the newly added package would adopt the old one's releases.
24	
25	## Consequences
26	
27	- Adding a same-named package changes new default tag names, but does not rename existing tags or move the CHANGELOG. Historical bare tags and pre-release baselines are assigned through the ownership fallback; rename, manifest-roster and demotion gaps are tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
28	- Workspaces that are already promoted keep their `cargo/foo@*` tags unchanged.
29	- Ownership costs one `git rev-parse` per candidate tag of a promoted package.
30	- A pending changeset that names the bare `foo` is ambiguous after promotion (E103, WS-ID-06) and must be qualified.
31	
32	## Enforcement
33	
34	- `TagTemplate::default_for` in `crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs`; the ownership fallback in `TagIndex::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`); `assign_promoted_pre_keys` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`.
35	- `promotion_changes_the_display_id_but_not_the_key` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`; `crates/callisto-cli/tests/identity_promotion_tests.rs`.
36	- WS-ID-03 and WS-ID-08 in `docs/specs/workspace.json`.
37	
38	## Revisit when
39	
40	- Something persists a package reference that is not a selector, tag or path, such as a cache keyed by package. It should use `PackageKey`.
41	- A package can move directories while keeping its identity.
42	
43	## Sources
44	
45	- Owner decision, `docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
46	- #167 ("refactor(identity)!: key packages by directory; promotion is display-only") and its zero-config follow-up

1	# Package identity
2	
3	How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).
4	
5	## Terms
6	
7	- Dual-manifest package: one directory with several admitted canonical manifests; one graph package, one version grammar and several distribution identities. Cargo+npm is supported by the model; co-located Cargo+Python currently fails with E007 because their grammars differ, including a Maturin dynamic Python version.
8	- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
9	- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.
10	
11	## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)
12	
13	| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
16	| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo:foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |
17	
18	- `parse` treats text before the first `:` or `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare.
19	- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
20	- `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name.
21	- Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11).
22	- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
23	  - Different names never match.
24	  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
25	  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
26	- A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership.
27	
28	## Resolving ambiguity
29	
30	A workspace can hold `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion. Canonical-only new references are planned in [the v1 design](polyglot-v1.md), not implemented by today's parser.
31	
32	- `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. Some status helpers still use `PackageId::resolve_unique`, a scan over display ids; these are not equivalent for dual-manifest packages with different native names.
33	- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: two linear passes over the rules in declaration order, prefixed rules first, then bare. It never sorts the rules. A bare rule that reaches a promoted name is an `AmbiguousName` error, using `ResolvedConfig::promoted_siblings`.
34	- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.
35	
36	## Loading a workspace
37	
38	`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):
39	
40	1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
41	2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
42	3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids, then names promoted into several ecosystems are recorded as `promoted_siblings`.
43	4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.
44	
45	## Historical ownership
46	
47	For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `sole_owner_at` checks which same-named candidate's first current canonical manifest path exists at the tag's commit; it does not read every historical manifest name. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies that ownership check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner.
48	
49	This is not complete rename, manifest-addition or demotion support. Removing a sibling can stop lookup of a newer qualified tag, and current paths can misidentify historic bare ownership. Those failures remain tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md); do not infer migration safety from the directory key alone.
50	
51	## Platform packages in code

61	
62	- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
63	- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
64	- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.
