  ## D01 tag-template research report
  
  I read the repo files and the primary docs for each comparable tool. No cargo runs, no repo edits.
  
  ### 1. Current Callisto behavior (read from code and docs)
  
  - **Default template.** `TagTemplate::default_for(id)` renders `{id.display_name()}@{version}` (`crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs:72`).
    - A bare id gives `foo@1.0.0`. A promoted id gives `cargo/foo@1.1.0`.
    - The doc comment on `default_for` still says "native name, so promotion never changes its tags". The code and its own unit test `default_for_qualifies_a_promoted_package` say the opposite. The comment is stale.
  - **Where tags are created.** `add_tags` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs` loops over owned release points: one per graph package, not per group.
    - A package gets a tag only if it has at least one publish target other than `none`.
    - Fixed groups do not change tag shape. There is no group-level tag in the code I read. Each published member gets its own `{template}` tag.
    - This repo's own history matches: `callisto-vcs@0.8.0`, `callisto-moon@0.8.0` and others sit beside `callisto@0.8.0` and later.
  - **Dual Cargo+npm package.** It is one graph package with one `PackageId`, taken from the primary manifest's name.
    - It gets one physical tag from that id. `tag_prerequisites` makes the tag wait for the registry publishes of every release identity.
    - Cargo and npm names are not both consulted, so a dual package with differing native names is tagged by the primary name only.
  - **GitHub release naming.** The forge release is created with `gh release create <tag> --verify-tag --draft` and no `--title`. The release name therefore follows the tag. I did not confirm gh's default-title behavior against its docs.
  - **CLI product tag.** `callisto.toml` sets `tag-template = "callisto@{version}"` and `previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]` on `cargo/callisto-cli`. This is explicit config, not a default.
  - **Last-tag lookup order** (`TagIndex::build`, `crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`), each step only if the previous found nothing:
    1. The package's template.
    2. `previous-tag-templates`, in order.
    3. For a promoted package with no explicit template: bare `{name}@` tags, kept only if `history::sole_owner_at` gives a unique owner.
    4. For a demoted package: qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem, keeping the newest across both families.
  - **E101.** `reject_shared_default_templates` fails when a package using the default template shares its rendered template with any other package.
    - The spec wording (WS-ID-08) says "explicit template equals another's default". The code condition is `has_default && ids.len() > 1`.
    - Two packages with identical explicit templates are allowed.
  - **`callisto init`** (`crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/init.rs`) probes four conventions: `{name}@`, `{name}-v`, `{name}-`, and `v{version}`. It writes an explicit `tag-template` for any non-default match.
    - It errors on ambiguous matches (`InitTagTemplateAmbiguous`) and on `v{version}` found for more than one package (`InitSharedVersionTag`).
  - **Constraints already in the docs.**
    - ADR 11 rejected "native name for every package" because promoted `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` would share tags (E101), and because already-promoted workspaces would change tag names.
    - ADR 12, still proposed, lists "collision-triggered bare/qualified identity" as an option it considered and did not choose (it says that option retains inference rules at every new consumer). It also says to preserve historical tag ownership and not use promotion as an identity change.
    - polyglot-v1 says not to rename existing tags to canonicalize selectors.
    - Plan task T06 says to settle new default tags and legacy rules, apply D01's rename/move boundary, and not rename remote tags or infer a move.
  
  ### 2. Comparable tools (sourced)
  
  | Tool | Per-package default | Fixed or single-package default | Collision and history handling |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Changesets | `pkg-name@version` in monorepos | `v1.0.0` in single-package repos. Source: `tool.type !== 'root' ? name@version : v<version>`. | Fixed and linked groups are version-only; the fixed-packages doc says nothing on tags. Name uniqueness comes from the npm namespace, and there is no ecosystem qualifier. [docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/changesets/changesets/main/docs/command-line-options.md), [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/changesets/changesets/main/packages/cli/src/commands/git-tag/utils.ts), [fixed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/changesets/changesets/main/docs/fixed-packages.md) |
  | release-please | `<component>-v<version>` | `include-component-in-tag: false` gives `v<version>`. Schema defaults: `include-component-in-tag` true, `include-v-in-tag` true. | Config is keyed by directory path. Component is explicit, except node, which reads it from the source. A tag mismatch gives "Expected 1 releases, only found 0", fixed with `bootstrap-sha`/`last-release-sha` overrides. There is no ecosystem qualification. [manifest docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md), [schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/main/schemas/config.json) |
  | Nx release | `{projectName}@{version}` (independent) | `v{version}` (fixed). Placeholders are `{version}`, `{projectName}` and `{releaseGroupName}`. Nx 22+ nests this as `release.releaseTag.pattern`, and Nx 23 removed the flat `releaseTagPattern*` keys. | The docs say to include `{projectName}` so each tag is unique. Per the source summary, `getLatestGitTagForPattern` uses one pattern with no legacy fallback, and `sanitizeProjectNameForGitTag` rewrites invalid characters. [nx.json](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [independent](https://nx.dev/docs/guides/nx-release/release-projects-independently), [git.ts](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/blob/master/packages/nx/src/command-line/release/utils/git.ts) |
  | Lerna | `pkg@x.y.z` (independent) | `vX.Y.Z` (fixed). `--tag-version-prefix` must be passed to both `version` and `publish`. | [docs](https://github.com/lerna/lerna/blob/main/libs/commands/version/README.md) |
  | cargo-release | `{{prefix}}v{{version}}`. `tag-prefix` defaults to `""` at the repo root and `{{crate_name}}-` in a subdirectory. | `shared-version` only syncs versions. `tag-name`, `tag-prefix` and `tag` are per-crate by default. | [reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/crate-ci/cargo-release/master/docs/reference.md) |
  | cargo-workspaces | Individual tags `%n@<version>` | Global tag `v<version>`. Both are on by default. `--no-individual-tags` and `--no-global-tag` turn each off. | [repo](https://github.com/pksunkara/cargo-workspaces) |
  | Knope | `<package>/v<version>` with several packages | `v<version>` with a single package | [tutorial](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/) |
  | semantic-release | None. `tagFormat` defaults to `v${version}`, must contain version exactly once, and is the only way it finds previous releases. | Monorepo guidance not found in the page I could fetch. | [config](https://semantic-release.gitbook.io/semantic-release/usage/configuration) |
  | Go modules | `subdir/vX.Y.Z` (for example `gopls/v0.6.0`). A v2+ module in `sub` uses `sub/v2.0.0`. | Root module tags are `vX.Y.Z`. | The tag prefix is the subdirectory path, so directory-keyed tags are native to Go. [go.dev/ref/mod](https://go.dev/ref/mod) |
  | setuptools-scm | None. `tag.prefix`, for example `hatchling-v`, filters via `git describe --match` and is stripped before parsing. A `tag.regex` is also available. | Default regex accepts an optional dashed-word prefix. | [config](https://setuptools-scm.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config/) |
  
  **Findings across tools**
  - Every tool uses `<native name><sep><version>` per package. None qualifies the tag by ecosystem.
  - Where the tool's own tag has no name part (`v<version>`), that is the fixed or single-package form.
  - Go is the only tool whose tag is derived from the directory. The directory is also what Go uses as module identity.
  - release-please keys its config by directory but names tags from an explicit or source-derived component.
  - No tool I checked reads old-pattern tags automatically after a pattern change.
    - Nx, per the source summary, does not.
    - semantic-release and release-please require the tag to match the configured format, and release-please offers manual SHA overrides.
    - Callisto's `previous-tag-templates` plus the ownership fallback is more than the field offers.
  - Cross-package collisions are avoided by name uniqueness within one ecosystem, or by user-written templates.
  
  **Not verified**
  - How Nx handles scoped npm names with `/`.
  - Whether Nx has a "legacy tag" mode. I found none in the docs, and the source summary says there is no fallback.
  - Changesets' fixed-group tagging beyond the per-package rule.
  - Knope's tag behavior for Cargo+Python in one package. The tutorial implies one tag per package.
  - Whether release-please derives the Rust or Python component automatically. The docs say only node does.
  - The semantic-release monorepo recipe.
  - How cargo-workspaces handles a name that exists in two ecosystems. It is Cargo-only.
  
  ### 3. Decision frame
  
  All five options keep old tags unrenamed, per the plan.
  
  | | T1 keep `{display id}@` | T2 native name, qualify on collision | T3 always `{eco}/{name}@` | T4 directory-key tag | T5 explicit config on first release |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Existing repos | Old tags resolve through current fallbacks. | Same as T1, with the collision rule moved into the template. | Bare history stays valid only through `previous-tag-templates` or the ownership fallback. Every repo gets a new tag namespace on its next release. | All history needs a fallback, including `previous-tag-templates`. | Unchanged until a template is written. Without one the first release must error or ask. |
  | Promoted dual package (same name in two ecosystems) | Tag namespace flips from `foo@` to `cargo/foo@` on promotion. That is today's behavior. | Same flip. | No flip. `cargo/foo@` and `npm/foo@` are distinct. | No flip. | Explicit, so no flip. |
  | Collision and E101 | E101 stays, and is needed. | E101 is the collision-trigger itself. | E101 cannot fire between ecosystems, but it still fires for two packages in one ecosystem with the same name, or two explicit templates equal to a default. | Never collides. | The user owns collisions. |
  | Human readability | Best for bare names. The promoted form is longer. | Same. | Longest. `cargo/callisto-model@0.8.0` matches Callisto's canonical-ID direction, but ordinary users see `cargo/` on every tag. | Poorest. `crates/foo@1.0.0` leaks layout. | Depends on the user. |
  | GitHub release name and registry version | Release name follows the tag and the registry stays `foo`. | Same. | The release name carries `cargo/foo` while the registry says `foo`. | The release name carries a path. | Depends on the user. |
  | Fixed groups | One tag per member, as today. A shared `v{version}` needs an explicit template. | Same. | Same, more verbose. | Same. | Same. |
  | Dual Cargo+npm owner | One tag from the primary name. Which ecosystem prefix applies depends on the primary-manifest rule. | The same primary-name issue. | The ecosystem prefix is ambiguous (Cargo or npm?), so the primary-manifest rule becomes a user-visible tag rule. | Natural fit, one directory and one tag. | The user picks. |
  | Go and NuGet | Go `subdir/v1.2.3` needs an explicit template. | Same. | Native only by chance (`go/subdir@` is not a Go tag). Still needs explicit config. | Closest to Go's subdir prefix, but still needs the `v` before the version. | Works for everything. |
  | Second inference authority | Yes. Collision-triggered promotion decides the namespace. | Yes, plus the rule now sits in `default_for` rather than only the display id. | No. Qualification is deterministic and needs no sibling scan. | No. | No. |
  
  T3 is the only option with no second inference authority and no namespace flip, but it changes every repo's next-release tag name. T1 and T2 keep the status quo and its flip.
  
  ### 4. Owner questions
  
  1. Default for new releases: always-qualified (T3), collision-triggered (T1/T2), or explicit-first-release (T5)? ADR 11 rejected "native name for every package" only because of E101 and tag renames. It never considered "qualify every package".
  2. If T3: for a dual Cargo+npm package, which ecosystem prefix goes on the one shared tag? Options are the primary manifest's ecosystem, a configured default, or a fixed priority (cargo over npm).
  3. Legacy tags under T3: keep the current fallbacks (`previous-tag-templates` plus ownership) as a permanent compatibility reader, or require `previous-tag-templates` on first v1 run? Should `init` write it automatically from observed tags, as it does for the four conventions today?
  4. Fixed groups: keep one tag per published member (today's behavior), or add a group-level tag (`v{version}`, as Nx, Lerna and cargo-workspaces do for fixed releases)? If a group tag is added, how does it interact with the explicit `[[package]]` template on `cargo/callisto-cli` and with `callisto-cli@` history?
  5. E101 semantics: should it fire when two packages share any rendered template (current code), or only for "explicit equals default" (the spec wording)? Settle that before changing the default. The spec and code disagree today.
  6. Go and NuGet: is a template-per-package escape hatch (explicit `tag-template = "subdir/v{version}"`) enough, or must the default itself be directory-prefixed? Callisto's template language has no `{dir}` placeholder, and `parse` requires a literal `{version}` anchor.
  7. The stale `default_for` doc comment should be fixed whichever way D01 lands.
  
  I did not confirm `gh release create`'s default title behavior, or how fixed-group tags behave when member packages have `publish-to = none`, beyond reading `add_tags`.

  ## D01 evidence: historical release ownership (binary callisto 0.11.0, worktree d1f0de357)
  
  Scratch repos and scripts: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/history/` (`lib.sh`, `run1.sh`, `run3.sh`, `run4.sh`, repos `s0`..`s7`, `a*`, `g*`). A stray copy of `run2.sh` landed under `/private/tmp/claude-501/claude-501/...` from a path typo. All scenarios used `callisto --format json status` (plus `version --dry-run` and `release --dry-run` where noted), real `git tag -a`, and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`.
  
  ### Headline
  SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION and the silent pre.json drop are already fixed on this main. The register text in `docs/projects/V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the "Conflicting pre-state aliases" row) and `V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json` is stale on these points. R2, the plan's choice, is mostly shipped (#230). The real remaining hole is that a package whose own id is bare, or whose tag lookup never reaches the ownership check, adopts a bare tag by name alone, and a sibling renamed into the shared name can steal a tag. That is a wrong-owner failure, not only a lost tag.
  
  ### Findings
  
  **1. SYS-OWNER (lost tag after sibling add, dir move or new primary manifest) does not reproduce.**
  - [REPRODUCED] S1: cargo `foo` tagged `foo@1.0.0`, npm `foo` added, `crates/foo` moved. Result: `cargo/foo last=1.0.0`, `npm/foo last=None`.
  - [REPRODUCED] S2: npm-first dir `foo@1.0.0`, pypi `foo` added, cargo manifest added beside npm. Result: `cargo/foo last=1.0.0`, `pypi/foo last=None`.
  - [SOURCE crates/callisto-graph/src/history.rs:84-117] `sole_owner_at` now falls back to the manifest roster at the tag commit, matched against each candidate's own native name via `IdentityIndex`.
  - [SOURCE tags.rs:210-229] and #230 (`55cb2107c`) fixed it. Tests are in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/identity_promotion_tests.rs:198-340`.
  
  **2. SYS-DEMOTION (newer qualified tag lost) does not reproduce.**
  - [REPRODUCED] S4: `foo@1.0.0`, npm added, `cargo/foo@1.1.0`, npm removed. Result: `foo last=1.1.0`.
  - [SOURCE tags.rs:230-244] A demoted package reads the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest across both families.
  
  **3. pre.json conflicting alias is no longer silent.**
  - [REPRODUCED] G1: `pre.json` added while cargo `foo` was the only `foo`, npm `foo` added later, then `cargo/foo:1.1.0` added beside `foo:1.0.0`. Result: E305 "records `foo` at 1.0.0 and `cargo/foo` at 1.1.0, but both name the same package". Equal versions are accepted.
  - [SOURCE lib.rs:365-384] `ConflictingPreJsonBaselines` is checked before any move (#222, `97fa03fc4`). The `or_insert` at lib.rs:388 is only reached when versions are equal.
  - If both keys exist and `pre.json` was added when both packages already existed, you get E245 (no sole owner), not E305.
  
  **4. Remaining defect: name-only adoption by a package with a bare id.** Wrong owner, silent, reproduces today.
  - [SOURCE tags.rs:184-192, 210] A package with a bare id (not promoted) looks up `foo@*` by name with no ownership check. The ownership fallback only runs when `pkg.id.ecosystem().is_some()`. The demotion block (230-244) adds only qualified tags.
  - [REPRODUCED] S3: npm `foo` owns `foo@1.0.0`, cargo `foo` 0.1.0 is added and never released, then npm `foo` is renamed to `bar`. Before the rename `cargo/foo` is None and `npm/foo` is 1.0.0. After it, bare `foo` (cargo, 0.1.0) reports `lastTag foo@1.0.0`.
  - [REPRODUCED] S5: same with npm removed instead of renamed. Cargo `foo` 0.1.0 reports `lastTag foo@5.0.0`.
  - [REPRODUCED] S6, native rename: cargo `foo` tagged `foo@1.0.0`, npm `foo` added, cargo renamed to `foo-core`. Npm `foo` 3.0.0 now owns `foo@1.0.0`, while the real owner `foo-core` shows `last=None`.
    - With `release-trigger = "auto"` and A6, `foo-core` plans a 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 patch bump from 2 replayed commits.
    - `release --dry-run` plans `cargo/foo-core 1.0.0` as `unreleasedVersion`.
  - docs/architecture/identity.md:55 states a native rename needs `previous-tag-templates`. It does not say a lookalike bare package will adopt the old tag instead of refusing.
  
  **5. Remaining defect: path-existence short-circuit is unsound.**
  - [SOURCE history.rs:93-103] If a candidate's current first-manifest path exists at the tag commit, it wins without checking what name that manifest declared then.
  - [REPRODUCED] S7: cargo `foo` is the real tag owner at `crates/old`, and `packages/b` was npm `bar` at tag time. Later `bar` is renamed `foo` and `crates/old` moves to `crates/a`. Result: `npm/foo last=1.0.0` (stole it) and `cargo/foo last=None`. `release --dry-run` then plans `cargo/foo 1.0.0` as unreleased.
  - Registry observation (ADR 3) adopts an already-published crate, which limits the harm at publish time. The wrong last tag still skews commit-inference windows and `lastReleasedVersion`.
  
  **6. Same hole in pre.json.**
  - [SOURCE lib.rs:323-334] When no promoted same-named package exists, a bare key goes through `identity.resolve` with no historical check.
  - [REPRODUCED] G2: `pre.json` bare `foo:1.0.0` was recorded for cargo `foo`. Cargo is then renamed `foo-core` and npm `foo` 3.0.0 is added. `version --dry-run` with a minor changeset on `foo` gives bump `foo 3.0.0 -> 1.1.0-beta.0`, a backwards version from the other package's baseline, with no error.
  - [REPRODUCED] G3 (move after sibling add) resolves correctly.
  
  **7. What a tag and the commit actually carry.**
  - [SOURCE derive.rs:551] A Callisto tag annotation is only `Release {tag_name}`.
  - [REPRODUCED] `git cat-file -p callisto@0.11.0` shows only that text, the commit, and the tagger. It carries no package id, roster or version beyond the tag name.
  - [SOURCE ADR 9] Annotation text is deliberately not compared and not a contract. Making it a durable record would conflict with ADR 9's "Revisit when" trigger.
  - [REPRODUCED] The tagged release commit holds the committed decision. `git show 5e8c1696e:.callisto/release-decision.json` lists `package: "cargo/callisto-cli"` (ReleasePackageId, native name), `targetVersion: "0.11.0"` and the reasons.
  - [SOURCE ADR 2; release.json:329] The decision is committed in the release PR at `decision_path` (default `.callisto/release-decision.json`) and is retained in git history. The tag target is the release commit (derive.rs:540-546), so `git show <tag>:<decision>` yields an owner roster per release.
  - Limits: it exists only for releases made through the release-PR flow (post-#54), the path is configurable, and it records the old native name but no link to a new name after a rename.
  
  **8. Information available at a historic commit.**
  - The tree: manifests, `callisto.toml`, changelog paths, `pre.json`, and the decision file when present.
  - Cost (from the #230 message): the roster fallback is about 275 git calls and 3 s for 200 packages and 30 tags, using `git grep`.
  - Cost of R1: one existence check per candidate per tag. The commit message ties the roster fallback to `files_containing_at` and `read_at` in `GitAccess`.
  
  ### Prior art
  - [WEB https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md]
    - release-please searches tags `<component>-v<version>`. `include-component-in-tag:false` searches `v<version>`.
    - The doc also says it reads the manifest at the commit of the last merged release PR, so state is a committed file keyed by path rather than tag text.
    - Escape hatches for missing tags: `bootstrap-sha` and `last-release-sha`, both explicit user declarations.
  - [WEB https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json]
    - Nx release has one `releaseTag.pattern`, and the legacy flat keys were removed in Nx 23.
    - With no tag matching the pattern on the current branch, it falls back to checking all branches unless `checkAllBranchesWhen` is false.
    - A search result indicates `fallbackCurrentVersionResolver:'disk'` is the explicit opt-in for no-tag projects. I did not fetch a primary page for that.
    - Nx does not infer ownership from old patterns.
  - [WEB https://github.com/crate-ci/cargo-release/blob/master/docs/reference.md] cargo-release has `tag-prefix` (default `{{crate_name}}-` outside the repo root), `tag-name`, and a per-run `--prev-tag-name`. Previous-tag overrides are explicit.
  - [WEB https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts] changesets builds a publish plan from changeset metadata and package versions, not from prior tags. Tags are created after publish.
  - Not verified: Knope's docs page gave no answer on last-tag lookup, and the Lerna doc page was inconclusive. I could not fetch either's source. I found no release-please issue text on renamed components.
  - Pattern across the tools I could verify: none infers a prior owner after a rename, and each uses a committed file (release-please) or an explicit override (cargo-release, Nx).
  
  ### Scenario x rule matrix
  Cells are what each rule would do, not a ranking. R1 is shipped. R2 is half shipped (the manifest roster fallback exists, but it runs only for promoted and demoted packages, and the path check still short-circuits it). "Loud" means a refusal.
  
  | Scenario | R1 path exists | R2 roster and native names at tag commit | R3 decision at tag commit | R4 explicit declaration | R5 freeze, no auto-adopt |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Sibling added (promotion) | OK | OK | OK if a decision exists | not needed | loud, needs config |
  | Dir moved | misses, then roster falls back to OK today | OK | OK (native name) | not needed | loud |
  | New primary manifest in an npm-first dir | misses, then roster falls back to OK today | OK | OK | not needed | loud |

     | `schemaVersion` 3 | E166 "unsupported ... version 3; this build reads versions [1, 2]" |
     | New `owner` field on an entry | E166 "unknown field `owner`, expected `package`, `targetVersion`, `reasons`" |
     | New top-level unknown field | E166 |
     | Unknown reason `kind` | E166 "unknown variant" |
  
     Every durable type under crates/callisto-model/src/release/ uses `deny_unknown_fields`. Serde `#[serde(default)]` therefore only helps new readers read old files. Old readers reject any new field even when it is optional.
  
  5. **[REPRODUCED] Scenarios.** Real binary used `release plan` and `--dry-run` in scratch repos.
     - **Dual Cargo/npm owner: handled.**
       - The CI route's decision has both `cargo/dual` and `npm/dual`.
       - The one tag, forge release and forge publish sit on `cargo/dual`.
       - The tag waits on both registry publishes.
       - Unit test `a_dual_owners_shared_tag_and_release_wait_for_both_registry_publishes` (derive.rs:1906) covers the order-independence.
     - **Platform packages: handled by source and snapshot only, not rerun.**
       - `PlatformPublish` operations are keyed by the owner id.
       - The platform directory is already on the wire in `PlatformPackageV1.directory` (crates/callisto-model/src/release/operation.rs:~101).
       - They are prerequisites of the owner's registry publish (derive.rs:375-410 and snapshot `derived_npm_owner_with_a_platform_package_is_pinned`).
     - **Fixed group: handled.** Each member keeps its own tag, forge release and forge publish, with no sharing.
     - **Product plus plugin artifact: partly handled, one edge to flag.**
       - The product's forge publish waits for the draft and for every upload, including the plugin's asset.
       - Neither the plugin's asset upload nor the product's forge publish waits for the plugin's own registry publish or tag.
       - If the owner wants "public announcement waits for every output on the release", this is an extra prerequisite edge. It is a DAG change and needs no new field.
     - **Cargo+Maturin co-located: not supported today.**
       - `status` and `release --dry-run` both fail with E007 ("disagreeing version grammars [Pep440, SemVer]"), for both static and `dynamic = ["version"]` pyproject.
       - This is the open SYS-MATURIN finding and spec WS-ID-09, which is a version-authority problem.
       - The wire already carries a per-entry native `targetVersion` parsed with the entry's ecosystem grammar, and `pypi/<name>` operations already drive `matrix_workflow.tmpl:84`.
       - Separate-directory Maturin layouts load as two independent packages (walk/tests.rs:1130).
     - **Wrong result found: partial selection of a dual package.**
       - `release --dry-run --package npm/dual` plans a tag, forge release and forge publish after only the npm publish. `--package cargo/dual` does the same after only the Cargo publish.
       - The cause is `expand_selection`, which filters by exact id (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:140).
       - After a tag exists on an older commit, the sibling is stranded. `release --dry-run` says "Nothing to release." and `--package npm/dual` gives E169.
       - A rerun at the same HEAD recovers it through `incomplete_tagged_releases` (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/local.rs:105). I did not run that path, because it observes registries over the network.
       - release.md:101 documents this as current behavior.
       - The fix is to make selection package-granular (expand to all release ids of a graph package) or reject partial selection. A persisted owner field would not fix it.
     - The CI route always writes one entry per canonical manifest (VER-APPLY-10), so it cannot produce a partial dual roster.
  
  6. **Announcement and draft timing: already settled by shipped behavior.**
     - The DAG is registry publishes, then tag, then forge draft (`gh release create --draft`, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/forge.rs:89-102), then artifact uploads, then forge publish (`gh release edit --draft=false`, forge.rs:~185).
     - The draft is stricter than the ADR's "may be preparatory". It is created only after every registry publish and the tag, because the tag is its prerequisite (derive.rs:562-612, 716-760).
     - Specs REL-ORD-01 and REL-GH-02 state this, and the dual test above proves it.
     - A rerun finishes a tagged but incomplete release (REL-RERUN-02, local.rs:105-143).
     - What remains open is only the product-plus-plugin edge in finding 5.
  
  7. **[SOURCE] The project already has a versioning precedent.** See the table below; the decision reader accepts N-1, and intents are hard-cut.
     - Intents went 3, 4, 5 with the changelog line "re-plan intents made by older versions" (crates/callisto-cli/CHANGELOG.md:139, 197). This is a de facto hard cut, enforced by `read_intent` (crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs:651-667, E215) and by re-derivation (capability.rs:287).
     - The decision went 1 to 2 for the additive reason `unreleasedVersion`, with a reader accepting 1 and 2 (decision.rs:118-120, commit 7027bbfb0, fixture crates/callisto-model/tests/fixtures/release-decision-v1-0.8.0.json).
     - The decision digest excludes `schemaVersion` (docs/architecture/wire-compat.md), so v1 and v2 decisions with the same entries share a digest.
     - Two additive precedents shipped without a bump:
       - `ArtifactManifestV1.distributions`, with `skip_serializing_if = Vec::is_empty` (artifact.rs:185). Old content serializes byte-identically, so the manifest digest is unchanged.
       - The envelope's optional `artifact_manifest_digest` (execution.rs:57).
  
  8. **Existing documentation.** docs/architecture/wire-compat.md (#217) already enumerates reader policy and known gaps. The D01 "Wire compatibility" row in docs/projects/V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md asks for an enumeration that already exists; only the old-intent rerun policy needs recording as owner policy.
  
  ### Wire documents
  
  | Document | Struct | Version | Digest/seal | Identity fields | Reader policy | Consumers |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Decision `ReleaseDecisionV1` (`.callisto/release-decision.json`) | crates/callisto-model/src/release/decision.rs:~88 | writes 2, reads [1,2] (:118-120) | SHA-256 over sorted entries, excludes version (:~163) | `ReleasePackageId` strings, per-entry native `targetVersion` | strict `deny_unknown_fields`, E166 | `release plan --from-release-commit` (release_decision.rs:377), intent embeds it |
  | Snapshot `ReleaseInputSnapshotV1` | snapshot.rs:37 | 1 | semantic-input digest | `ReleasePackageId` plus fingerprint | only the intent decoder checks the version | inside the intent only |
  | Intent `ReleaseIntentV1` (`release plan --out`) | intent.rs:13 | 5, exact | intent digest over decision digest, snapshot digest, operations, prerequisites, slots | `ReleasePackageId`, registry binding id, platform name and directory | strict, E215 or E295, then re-derivation E124 | `release execute`, `artifact-manifest`, simulator (`SimWorld`), jq in the workflows |
  | Artifact manifest `ArtifactManifestV1` | artifact.rs:178 | 1 | canonical serialization hash | slot (`ReleasePackageId`), `DistributionSetV1.package` | strict fields, no decode-time version gate | `artifact-manifest`, `execute` (E237) |
  | Envelope `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` | execution.rs:51 | 3 | binds the intent digest and manifest digest | commits only | exact version, `UnsupportedSchema` with no code | inside the receipt |
  | Receipt `ReleaseReceiptV1` | execution.rs:345 | 2 | intent digest | operation ids, provider evidence | exact version | `run-release.sh` (jq), `callisto schema --type release-receipt` |
  | `pre.json` | crates/callisto-model/src/format/pre.rs | none (changesets-compatible) | none | bare or display keys | hand-parsed, tolerant | version/pre commands |
  | Release-PR documents | release_pr.rs | 1 or 2 each | none | repository and branches | exact version, E155 | `release-pr` and the action script |
  
  Other facts:
  - Published JSON schemas cover only the receipt, status and similar reports (`callisto schema --type`). There are none for the decision, intent or manifest.
  - `release inspect` is a raw JSON passthrough with no version gate.
  - The shell readers in `matrix_workflow.tmpl` and `run-release.sh` depend on field shape: `.operations[].id.package`, `.artifactSlots`, `.outcomes[].operation`.
  
  ### Spec impact
  
  - **(a) Persisted owner field.**
    - VER-APPLY-10 and REL-AUTH-03 would change (decision shape and accepted versions).
    - REL-AUTH-06 would need an owner-equals-derivation check.
    - REL-CMD-12 and wire-compat.md would change. The decision digest transcript would change.
    - A field on `ReleaseDecisionEntry` makes every older reader E166, even at the same `schemaVersion`.
  - **(b) Canonical-only ids in decisions and intents:** already true, so there is no change.
  - **(c) Python as a Cargo owner's output:**
    - WS-ID-09 changes (E007).
    - REL-ORD-01 already says "registry publishes belonging to its canonical manifests".
    - REL-PUB-04/REL-GH-05 and the `distributions` manifest already carry per-file Python sets.
  - **Cost of a v2 bump.**
    - Open release PRs with a v2 decision stay readable if readers accept [1, 2, 3].
    - `verify` of committed history is safe because the reader accepts N-1, as the 0.8.0 fixture proves. A hard cut would break re-reading historical decisions unless readers keep [1, 2].
    - Mid-rerun intents: v5 intents already die across derivation changes, because ADR 3 reruns re-plan from the commit and no state is kept. A bump costs nothing extra there.
    - The real compatibility risk is the pinned action binary: a new decision with an old binary gives E166, which is fail-closed.
  
  ### Prior art
  
  - Terraform's JSON formats use `format_version` with a major.minor scheme. Readers ignore unknown properties on a minor bump and reject an unsupported major [WEB https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format]. The binary plan file must be applied by the same Terraform version [WEB https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/terraform-show-json/9778].
  - cargo-dist's dist-manifest has "epochs" (3 so far) and aims to stay forward and backward compatible, because one tool reads releases spread over years and self-hosts from older ones [WEB https://docs.rs/cargo-dist-schema]. I could not fetch the book page, so this is from search snippets.
  - Changesets `pre.json` has no version field; its shape is the `PreState` type in `@changesets/types` [WEB https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/prereleases.md].
  - release-please's manifest is a plain `{path: version}` map with no schema version [WEB search result only].
  - Callisto's closed-reader approach matches Terraform's major-bump rule, but has no minor lane.
  
  ### Options
  
  | | Cost | Risk and mid-flight | `verify` history |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **W1: no persisted owner, derive at plan time (current)** | Near zero. Fix partial-selection expansion, decide the plugin-barrier edge, record the owner rule in an ADR. | Re-derivation (E124) already fails closed on any owner or DAG change; old intents get re-planned. | Unchanged; history reads as today. |
  | **W2: add an optional field (serde default, skip when absent)** | Small code, but doubles the source of truth with derivation and needs a consistency check. | Old readers reject the new field (E166), so action-pinned older binaries break on any decision that carries it. | Old decisions fine for new readers. |
  | **W3: bump decision to 3, keep reading [1, 2, 3]** | Medium. Update VER-APPLY-10, REL-AUTH-03, wire-compat.md and the fixture. | Same old-binary E166 as W2; matches the 1 to 2 precedent. | Safe for history. |
  | **W4: hard cut (reject old decisions, intents and `pre.json`)** | Cheapest code. | Open release PRs with v2 decisions break; breaks the 0.8.0-style recovery. Rejecting `pre.json` would break changesets compatibility (ADR 1). | `verify` of history fails. |
  
  Recommendation: W1, with no bump now. If an explicit owner is ever needed, use W3 (bump the decision, keep reading [1, 2]), not W2, because W2 gives old readers a confusing E166 on an unknown field with no version number to point at. The decision on the intent's schema version is independent. If its operation vocabulary changes again, bump to 6 and rely on the existing E215 plus re-plan.
  
  ### Owner-only questions (either/or)
  
  1. Should the owner stay derived (Cargo, then npm, then PyPI) and be recorded in ADR 12 as such, or should an explicit field be added (W3)?
  2. Should `--package <one id of a dual package>` expand to the whole graph package, or be rejected with a "select all its identities" error? (It strands the sibling today.)
  3. Should a product release's public announcement wait for registry publishes of packages whose assets it carries (the plugin case), or only for the product's own publishes?
  4. Intent policy: keep "re-plan, never cross-version rerun" (ADR 3 plus E215) as the written rule, or add a v5 reader if the intent vocabulary changes again?
  5. For Cargo+Maturin, are Python and Cargo one graph package (two canonical manifests, per-entry native versions, which needs the grammar rule relaxed) or two packages sharing an owner label?
  
  ### Could not verify
  
  - Rerun recovery of a partially selected dual package (`incomplete_tagged_releases`) needs live registries.
  - Real publishes, GitHub draft behavior, a real Maturin build and a real npm platform package. The platform-package scenario is source and snapshot only.
  - The cargo-dist book page, release-please docs and Nx (fetch failed or not searched). The release-please and cargo-dist claims come from search snippets.
  - I did not run `release execute` or the simulator.

# D01 decision brief

Local only, never PR it. Evidence gathered 2026-10-20 on main `d1f0de357` (v0.11.0) with a real binary, scratch repos and five read-only research passes. Each claim is tagged: reproduced (real binary), source (file read), web (URL). I re-ran two of the reproductions myself (E007 and the bare-tag adoption in D01-D). Scratch repos and scripts: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/` (`maturin/`, `history/`, `refs/`, `wire/`, `verify/`).

## What the plan got wrong

The D01 table in `docs/projects/V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md` was written on 2026-09-26. Against v0.11.0:

| Plan row | Today |
| --- | --- |
| Owner identity: durable owner field vs derivation | Owner is already derived (first release id of the package by priority Cargo, npm, PyPI) and sealed in the intent digest. No field is needed (source: `release/derive.rs:258-295`, `capability.rs:287`) |
| Wire compatibility: new versions for owner/effect shape | Release wire is already canonical-only and strict. Nothing in the current scope needs a bump (reproduced: bare and colon ids give E166) |
| Announcement ordering | Shipped. Registry publishes, then tag, then draft, then uploads, then publish (source: `derive.rs:562-612`, `provider/forge.rs:89-102`) |
| Registry file set, Python destinations | Shipped (#232, #233, #249) |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Settled, nothing to do |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases (`or_insert` drops legacy) | Fixed. Different versions now give E305; equal versions are accepted (reproduced; #222) |
| SYS-OWNER, SYS-DEMOTION | No longer reproduce (reproduced S1, S2, S4; #230 added the roster fallback in `history.rs`) |
| Status helpers still use `resolve_unique` | Stale. It is `#[deprecated]` with no production caller |

Genuinely open: Maturin (D01-A), the reference boundary (D01-B), the tag default (D01-C), three residual ownership holes (D01-D) and two small release-graph choices (D01-E).

## D01-A: Maturin and native version authority

Reproduced: a directory holding `Cargo.toml` and a maturin `pyproject.toml` fails `status`, `version`, `snapshot`, `release` and `init` with E007, whether the Python version is dynamic, static, workspace-inherited or Cargo carries a prerelease. A separate-directory layout works, but Cargo and PyPI packages cannot be in a fixed or linked group (E107), so there is no lockstep in any layout. Dynamic Python versions are unsupported everywhere (a pyproject-only dynamic project gives E013). The E007 message lists the two grammars in a nondeterministic order (HashSet).

The plan's premise, "deterministic SemVer to PEP 440 mapping", is wrong. Maturin does not map. It parses the Cargo string directly as a PEP 440 version with `pep440_rs` 0.7.3, the same crate and version as Callisto's lockfile (web: maturin `src/metadata.rs`; reproduced with maturin 1.15.0 `pep517 write-dist-info`). Callisto does not write the Python version, so the question is a validation predicate, not a conversion. Callisto's own pre-release mapper (`format/bump.rs:164-211`) falls back to `.devN` for tags maturin rejects, so the two disagree.

| Cargo version | maturin result | Faithful? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1.2.3-alpha.1`, `-beta.2`, `-rc.1` | `1.2.3a1`, `b2`, `rc1` | yes |
| `-pre.1`, `-c.1`, `-rc.1` | all `rc1` | no, three SemVer versions collapse to one |
| `-dev.1` | `.dev1` | no, sorts below `a1`; SemVer sorts `dev` above `alpha` |
| `-post.1`, `-0`, `-1` | `.post1`, `.post0`, `.post1` | no, a SemVer prerelease becomes a post-release that sorts above the release |
| `-next.0`, `-canary.0`, `-my.tag.0`, snapshot `0.0.0-abc-e7efa2b` | error | unmappable |
| `+build.5` | local version `1.2.3+build.5` | PyPI rejects it; SemVer ignores build metadata |

Also reproduced: a static `project.version = "9.9.9"` next to Cargo `1.2.3` builds `9.9.9` silently. Both `version` and `dynamic = ["version"]` only warns in maturin 1.15 (PEP 621 says error). `uv lock --check` passes after a Cargo bump with a dynamic version. Not verified: a full wheel build and install, maturin before 1.15, release-please, cargo-release, Nx and cargo-dist behavior for Cargo-owned Python versions.

Code that assumes one grammar per package (source): `Package::version_grammar` (`package.rs:44-64`; callers `tags.rs:188`, `snapshot.rs:34`, `init.rs:314,329`), `base_versions` taking the first manifest (`lib.rs:210-234`), single-valued `PlannedBump` and `BumpRecord`, `write_version_guarded` writing one `to` to every manifest (`apply.rs:465-482`), `python::write_version` inserting `project.version` next to `dynamic` (`python.rs:453`), `VersionSource` having no dynamic variant (`manifests/lib.rs:46-49`), commit verification comparing `Version` across grammars (`release_decision.rs:534-541`; `Version` equality includes grammar), group grammar check (`groups.rs:49`). The wire already carries a native `targetVersion` per distribution entry, so no wire change is implied.

Options:

| | Behavior | Cost | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 allow-list, dynamic only | One package, Cargo is the authority. Python version is derived with the same parser as maturin and verified. Accept stable and `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, `-rc.N`. Refuse every other prerelease form, build metadata and snapshots for a co-located PyPI output, before any write. A static `project.version` next to Cargo is refused (maturin does not catch drift) | Large. Model, manifests, graph per the list above, plus a built-wheel metadata check | Cargo users lose `next`/`canary`/custom pre tags on co-located packages. The allow-list is verified against maturin 1.15.0 only |
| A2 allow-list, static allowed | Same, but a static `project.version` equal to the derived value is also accepted and Callisto rewrites both | Larger. Two writers, the grammar-per-write problem in `apply.rs`, and `uv.lock` refresh | Two sources of truth that can drift |
| A3 keep E007 | Stay out of scope for v1. Fix the nondeterministic grammar order and make the help text say "use separate directories". No lockstep Cargo+PyPI | Small | The headline Rust-to-Python path stays manual, with silent crate/wheel skew possible |
| A4 two packages in one directory | `Package::key` is the directory and the walker, tags, changelog and promotion assume one package per directory | Very large | Identity model change; E100/E101 interactions |

Lean: A1 if Maturin is in the v1 promise, otherwise A3 plus the small E007 fix. A2 and A4 add cost without a matching benefit. Owner questions: (1) is the allow-list acceptable, or must custom pre tags work for co-located packages; (2) refuse or ignore a static Python version that disagrees with Cargo; (3) refuse snapshots and `+build` for co-located PyPI outputs, or skip the PyPI output for them. Reports can keep the authority (SemVer) version only; the Python version lives in the decision entry. This is my inference from the wire shape, not verified.

## D01-B: canonical references and the legacy boundary

State today (reproduced and source):

| Surface | Accepts | Emits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release wire (decision, intent, snapshot, manifest, receipt) | `ecosystem/native-name` only | same |
| `release --package` | qualified only; bare gives E227; colon accepted as an alias | n/a |
| `product-package`, `[[release.artifact]] package` | qualified only; bare gives E197 | n/a |
| Changesets, `callisto add`, config groups and rules, `pre.json`, `matrix --package` | bare, `eco:name`, `eco/name` (prefix case-insensitive) | bare when unpromoted, slash when promoted |
| `status`, `version`, `matrix` output | n/a | bare when unpromoted, slash when promoted |
| `callisto init` | n/a | always slash |

Colon is emitted nowhere. The real trap is promotion: a changeset `foo: minor` works until an unrelated `npm/foo` appears, then `status` reports an ambiguous-package error (reproduced; WS-ID-06). It fails loudly, not silently.

Findings that change the scope:
- A changeset entry names an owner package, not a distribution. In a dual Cargo+npm directory `x-core`, `cargo/x-core`, `npm/@x/core` and `@x/core` all write `x-core: minor`, and an entry naming both merges into one bump (reproduced). "The canonical reference" for an entry has no single answer.
- Python selectors use the declared name (`pypi/Foo_Bar`); `foo-bar` and `pypi/foo-bar` give E102. PEP 503 normalization applies only to dependency-name lookup. Canonical-only must choose declared or normalized.
- ADR 1 promises one-commit adoption and rollback with `@changesets/cli`. Canonical `npm/@scope/x` in `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` breaks that for npm users. `pre.json` is also changesets-compatible.
- This repo dogfoods the bare forms: `callisto.toml` groups, all 8 `.changeset/*.md`, `AGENTS.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md` (`--package callisto-cli:<bump>`), and 111 bare tags.
- Blast radius if readers become strict: 166 colon literals in about 25 test files (mechanical), 192 bare `PackageId::parse` calls (mostly unit tests), roughly 26 bare `--package` args in CLI tests, and 24 of 236 spec criteria. T06 lists only 11 of them; WS-ID-07, WS-CFG-03/04/08, VER-PRE-01 and WS-ID-10 are missing.
- There is no `migrate` or `doctor` command and no config schema version (`RawConfig` is `deny_unknown_fields`). Only Nx (`nx migrate`) and Lerna (`lerna repair`) ship one among the tools checked (web, from search summaries; not verified on the primary pages).

Options for the legacy-read boundary:

| | Readers | Writers | Cost | Cost to users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 hard break | canonical only | canonical | Large: strict readers, 400+ fixtures, ~24 criteria | Every existing repo, this one included, fails on upgrade and users hand-edit. Breaks ADR 1 rollback |
| M2 warn, then canonical on write | legacy accepted with a warning | canonical | Medium: warning plumbing, a diagnostic code, format-preserving rewrites | Smooth; two spellings persist until a deadline |
| M3 explicit `callisto migrate` | strict after migration; old repos error with a pointer | canonical | Largest: new command, spec, tests, plus strict readers | Auditable one-command rewrite; adoption cost |
| M4 only change writers | unchanged | canonical | Smallest | None; leaves the promotion trap and contradicts "reject new bare aliases" |
| M5 split by surface | canonical required in config, groups, rules, reports, matrix keys, CLI args; changesets and `pre.json` keep native names and resolve at read time | canonical where unambiguous | Medium | Keeps ADR 1 interop; the promotion trap remains only in changesets, where it is loud |

Lean: M5, with colon rejected everywhere (never emitted, so nothing breaks) and an error that names the slash form. It keeps the owner's intent where identity matters (config, reports, CLI), respects ADR 1, and avoids a new command. If you want the owner text taken literally for every authored file, M3 is the only option with an auditable boundary and it should be scheduled as its own PR. Owner questions: (1) does canonical-only apply to changeset files and `pre.json`; (2) does it apply to report and matrix keys for unpromoted packages (a report `schemaVersion` bump); (3) `pypi/` form: declared name or PEP 503 normalized; (4) platform-manifest npm names in groups stay native, or get `npm/` forms; (5) keep ADR 1 interop for npm-only workspaces.

## D01-C: default tag template

Today: `TagTemplate::default_for` renders `{display id}@{version}`, so `foo@1.0.0` while unpromoted and `cargo/foo@1.1.0` after a same-named sibling appears. The doc comment above it (`tag.rs:70`) says the opposite and is stale. Tags are one per published package, fixed groups do not share a tag, and a dual Cargo+npm package gets one tag named from the primary manifest (source: `derive.rs` `add_tags`; `release.md:8,101`). Lookup order: the package's template, `previous-tag-templates`, the ownership fallback for promoted packages, then qualified tags for demoted ones (source: `tags.rs`). E101 in code fires when a default template is shared by any two packages (`has_default && ids.len() > 1`, `tags.rs:127-133`); the WS-ID-08 wording says "explicit template equals another's default". They disagree. `init` probes four conventions and writes an explicit template for any non-default match.

Prior art (web, primary docs, partly search summaries): every tool checked names tags `<native name><sep><version>` per package, with `v<version>` for a single or fixed unit. None qualifies a tag by ecosystem. Go is the only one that derives the tag from the directory (`subdir/vX.Y.Z`). No tool reads old-pattern tags automatically after a change; Callisto's `previous-tag-templates` plus ownership fallback already exceeds that.

| | Existing repos | Promoted package | Second inference authority | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- S5: same with npm removed. Cargo `foo` 0.1.0 reports `foo@5.0.0`.

What is maturin, tell me more

Maturin is a build tool for Python packages written in Rust. It compiles a Rust crate into a Python extension module and packages it as a wheel (`.whl`) or sdist that PyPI accepts.

**Why it exists**
- Python code that needs speed or native libraries is often written in Rust through PyO3 (the Rust-to-Python bindings) or rust-cpython. Examples are `ruff`, `pydantic-core`, `cryptography` and `polars`.
- Maturin is the PEP 517 build backend for those projects. A `pyproject.toml` with `build-backend = "maturin"` lets `pip install` or `uv build` compile the Rust code with no setup.py.
- It also handles other Rust-to-Python shapes: `cffi` and `uniffi` bindings, and plain Rust binaries shipped as wheels. It builds platform-tagged wheels (manylinux, musllinux, macOS universal2, Windows) and can cross-compile.

**Commands**
- `maturin develop` builds and installs into the current virtualenv, which is the inner dev loop.
- `maturin build` produces wheels.
- `maturin publish` uploads them.
- `maturin sdist` produces a source distribution.

**Why it matters for Callisto**
- A maturin project is one directory holding both `Cargo.toml` and `pyproject.toml`. It is one crate that publishes to crates.io and one wheel that publishes to PyPI.
- Maturin's metadata rules:
  - With no `[project]` table, everything comes from `Cargo.toml`.
  - With one, only fields listed in `dynamic` come from Cargo, usually `dynamic = ["version"]`.
  - Either way, the wheel version is the Cargo version.
- That causes the E007 failure I reproduced. Callisto requires one version grammar per package: SemVer for Cargo, PEP 440 for Python. Here the same directory carries both, with Cargo as the real authority.

**How its version handling works (what I verified)**
- Maturin does not convert SemVer to PEP 440. It parses the Cargo version string directly as a PEP 440 version.
  - So `1.2.3-alpha.1` becomes `1.2.3a1`.
  - Forms like `-next.0` fail.
  - `-pre.1`, `-c.1` and `-rc.1` all collapse to `rc1`.
  - `-dev.1` and `-post.1` change the sort order.
  - `+build` metadata gives a version PyPI rejects.
- I confirmed this with maturin 1.15.0's metadata hook only. I did not run a full wheel build or install.

That is why decision A in the brief is a validation allow-list, not a conversion.
What is pep 440 and pep 517?

Both are Python Enhancement Proposals, the standards documents that define how Python packaging works.

**PEP 440: version identification and dependency specification**

It defines what a valid Python package version looks like and how versions compare.

- Form: `[epoch!]release[aN|bN|rcN][.postN][.devN][+local]`.
- Examples:
  - `1.2.3`: a final release.
  - `1.2.3a1`, `1.2.3b2`, `1.2.3rc1`: alpha, beta and release candidate.
  - `1.2.3.post1`: a post-release, which sorts above `1.2.3`.
  - `1.2.3.dev1`: a dev release, which sorts below even `1.2.3a1`.
  - `1.2.3+abc.5`: a local version, for builds that are not public. PyPI rejects these.
- It normalizes spellings, so `alpha`, `c`, `pre` and `preview` become `a`, `rc`, `rc` and `rc`.
- It also defines version specifiers such as `>=1.2,<2` and `~=1.2`.

It differs from SemVer, which uses `1.2.3-alpha.1` and puts all prereleases below the release. PEP 440 has no `-next.0`. It also has post-releases, which SemVer lacks. That mismatch is the root of the Maturin problem: PEP 440 can't represent every SemVer prerelease, and some map to a different sort order.

In Callisto, PEP 440 is the version grammar for PyPI packages, and SemVer is the grammar for Cargo and npm. E007 fires when one package has manifests in both.

**PEP 517: a build-system interface for packaging**

It defines how a frontend (`pip`, `uv`, `build`) asks a build backend to build a package, without relying on `setup.py`.

- `pyproject.toml` declares the backend in a `[build-system]` table:
  ```toml
  [build-system]
  requires = ["maturin>=1,<2"]
  build-backend = "maturin"
  ```
- The frontend installs `requires` into an isolated environment, then calls standard hooks on the backend: `build_wheel`, `build_sdist` and a few metadata hooks.
- That makes the backend swappable: setuptools, hatchling, flit, poetry-core and maturin all implement the same interface.

Maturin is a PEP 517 backend, so `pip install .` or `uv build` on a Rust project just works. The hook I used in the research, `pep517 write-dist-info`, is maturin's command for writing package metadata. It reads `cargo metadata` without compiling, which is how I got maturin's real version output.

PEP 440 has a crate. PEP 517 does not really, and calling maturin as a library is possible but a poor fit.

**PEP 440**
- `pep440_rs` (0.7.3 on crates.io) implements versions and specifiers. Callisto already depends on it: `callisto-model` uses it, and its `Cargo.lock` resolves to 0.7.3.
- Maturin's `Cargo.toml` pins the same version, which is why my reproduction matched maturin on every input.
- Related crates: `pep508_rs` (dependency specifiers) and `uv-pep440` (uv's internal copy, versioned 0.0.x and marked internal).

**PEP 517**
- PEP 517 is a runtime protocol, not a data format. A frontend installs the build backend into an isolated Python environment and calls Python hooks such as `build_wheel`. A pure Rust crate can't implement that without running Python.
- `pyproject-toml` (0.13.7) parses `pyproject.toml`, including the `[build-system]` table and `[project]` metadata. Maturin uses it. It reads the declaration but doesn't run builds.
- uv has a PEP 517 frontend, but it is internal to uv and not a reusable crate. I haven't checked its code, so treat that as unverified.

**Calling maturin as a library**
- The `maturin` crate (1.15.0) is published and does have a library target. In principle Callisto could call it directly instead of shelling out.
- I would not rely on it:
  - Its library API is not a documented stable interface, so a minor bump could break us.
  - It pulls in a large dependency tree for a tool Callisto only needs to ask one question: what version will you build?
  - AGENTS.md also says ecosystem tools publish and own their own auth (ADR 4), and the plan keeps Callisto out of build logic.
- For D01-A, the question isn't how to call maturin. Maturin's version rule is already available through `pep440_rs`, which Callisto uses. The allow-list option validates the Cargo version with that crate, and a real `maturin` metadata run would only be a check in tests.

I haven't checked the maturin library's public surface in detail. Say so if you want that before deciding.

Noted: `pep440_rs` is the parser for D01-A, and I recorded that in the brief. Callisto computes the expected Python version with `pep440_rs::Version::from_str(cargo_version)`, which matches maturin exactly, and doesn't use its own `.devN` mapper for co-located packages. That also removes the maturin-library question.

One decision remains, and the crate doesn't settle it: which Cargo versions to let through. Parsing the same way as maturin doesn't make the result faithful. I measured these cases with maturin 1.15.0:
- `-pre.1`, `-c.1` and `-rc.1` all become `rc1`. Two distinct Cargo releases would then produce the same PyPI version.
- `-dev.1` and `-post.1` land on the wrong side of the stable release when sorted.
- `+build` metadata gives a version PyPI rejects.

The choice:
- **Strict allow-list (my lean):** accept stable and `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, `-rc.N`, and refuse the rest before any write. Cargo users lose custom pre tags like `next` on co-located packages.
- **Accept anything the crate parses, except local versions:** nothing is refused unnecessarily. But two Cargo versions can collapse to one PyPI version. Callisto's rerun logic treats an already-published matching file as landed, so a second release could look finished without uploading anything. I haven't checked whether the existing hash check would catch that, so I'd treat it as a risk.

Which do you want? The brief leans on the strict allow-list.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about marking crates deprecated on crates.io:

## Current Deprecation Methods

Setting `badges.maintenance.status = "deprecated"` in Cargo.toml and publishing a version allows crate indexing sites to recognize the crate as deprecated. However, there are limitations with this approach.

## Yank vs. Deprecation

The search results show an ongoing discussion in the Rust community about the differences:

- **Yanking**: Yanking all versions of a crate marks the crates.io page as "this crate has been yanked" and provides an immediate indication that the crate shouldn't be used.

- **Deprecation Badge**: The official Crates.io site doesn't show badges set in Cargo.toml, even though they are part of the spec. Additionally, lib.rs and other indexing sites respect the deprecated status badge and display it (for example, showing the crate name crossed out).

## Current Limitations

crates.io doesn't currently offer any way to mark a crate as "do not use" other than setting the README and description or yanking all versions. The community has requested an official way to mark independent versions or ranges of versions as deprecated with a message, but not as forceful as a yank.

The search results indicate this remains an open feature request rather than an official deprecation feature implemented in 2026.

# Cargo Manifest Reference on Badges and Maintenance Status

According to the Cargo manifest reference, the `[badges]` section is used for specifying status badges for package registries. Here's what it says about deprecation:

## Deprecation Status

Under the `maintenance` table in `[badges]`, one of the available status options is:

> **`deprecated`**: The maintainer does not recommend using this crate (the description of the crate can describe why, there could be a better solution available or there could be problems with the crate that the author does not want to fix).

## Example Usage

```toml
[badges]
maintenance = { status = "deprecated" }
```

## Important Note

The reference includes this caveat:

> Note: [crates.io](https://crates.io/) previously displayed badges next to a crate on its website, but that functionality has been removed. Packages should place badges in its README file which will be displayed on [crates.io](https://crates.io/) (see [the `readme` field](#the-readme-field)).

So while you can specify a `deprecated` maintenance status in the manifest, the badges are no longer displayed by crates.io itself—they should instead be included in the crate's README file for visibility.

input.prompt: What does cargo yank do and not do; what does it say about deleting, existing Cargo.lock files, and use cases?

result.output:
# What `cargo yank` Does and Doesn't Do

## What It Does
`cargo yank` **removes a previously published crate's version from the server's index**, preventing it from being selected in new dependency resolutions.

## What It Doesn't Do
- **Does not delete data** — The crate remains available for download via the registry's download link
- **Does not affect existing lockfiles** — Cargo will continue to use yanked versions if they're specified in a pre-existing `Cargo.lock` file
- **Does not affect direct downloads** — Existing lock files or direct downloads are not affected

## Key Behavior
> "Cargo will not use a yanked version for any new project or checkout without a pre-existing lockfile, and will generate an error if there are no longer any compatible versions for your crate."

## Legitimate Use Cases

Crates should only be yanked in **exceptional circumstances**:
- Accidental publishes
- Unintentional SemVer breakages
- Significantly broken and unusable crates

## NOT Recommended For

- **Security vulnerabilities** — [RustSec](https://rustsec.org/) is the preferred, less disruptive mechanism
- **Copyright/licensing/personal data issues** — Simply yanking may not suffice; contact the registry maintainers instead
- **Leaked credentials** — Yanking cannot prevent further spreading since existing lock files and direct downloads are unaffected

## Best Practice Workflow
> "A common workflow is to yank a crate having already published a semver compatible version, to reduce the probability of preventing dependent crates from compiling."

# Road to v1

Unshipped work only. Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). [Owner requirement](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [implementation and stacked-PR execution](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [scoped model and prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

## Scope and guardrails

- Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now, including concrete napi-rs and Cargo/Maturin layouts. Go and C#/.NET/NuGet are architecture examples only.
- Canonical native distribution references; deliberate legacy migration; separate release ownership and version authority.
- Reuse the dependency graph and operation DAG. Native dependency, build input and version coupling do not mean the same thing.
- Native tools/CI own building, packing and authentication. No universal package manager, build scheduler, public plugin platform, service graph or cross-registry transaction.
- Keep committed release authority and provider-observed recovery with no execution journal. Only execute receives registry secrets; no GitHub Environment or separate reviewer gate in this repo.
- Each implementation PR updates affected specs, tests and docs, with one changeset per independent user-facing topic. Future behavior is not inserted into current specs before its implementation.

## Sequence

The execution portfolio holds the remaining work as bounded units, including the D01 owner-contract checkpoint. The execution guide defines plugin routing, agent write ownership, serial Cargo verification and main-targeted stacked PRs under the existing CI trigger.

### 1. Correct the model in bounded changes

- D01: confirm exact ownership, compatibility, native authority and registry-output proof contracts before architectural code; existing-contract repairs do not wait for it.
- T06 and T06-HISTORY: canonical new references and legacy/history migration across selectors, config, groups, changesets, reports, pre-state and tags. Rename, manifest additions, promotion and demotion retain the right owner's history. [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) remains proposed until implementation.
- T07: supported version authority and native distribution representations. Cover co-located Cargo/Maturin with Cargo-owned dynamic Python version and inspect built metadata; do not insert a second static version or build a universal converter.
- T08: shared physical effect ownership, so one tag, draft, upload or publication referenced by several distributions is executed once. The tag already waits for every registry publish of its package, and a rerun after a failed push completes the release. Retain the committed roster and no-journal executor. A future Go source tag is publication, not a universal completion marker.

The plan is an implementation portfolio, not an approved future-behavior spec. Resolve wire/compatibility choices and update the matching area spec with implementation; do not treat architectural packets as fully gated implementer handoffs before D01.

### 2. Reconcile generated workflows

The generated build-matrix workflow builds and places napi addons only for packages in the release intent. Native lifecycle hooks remain package-owner-defined and outside Callisto's release-operation graph; Callisto does not inspect or alter them.

A native Python argv test does not imply a generated Maturin workflow or authenticated private-index observation.

### 3. Verify supported workflows and onboarding

Each implementation unit adds its own regression/fault tests. T12 integrates these representative cases through production/native paths; T12-DX measures onboarding:

| Fixture | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- |
| Cargo workspace | Inherited/root versions, renamed dependencies, locked resolution and index propagation |
| npm/pnpm | Workspace ranges, aliases, paths, catalogs, peer/optional/private policy and packed metadata |
| Python | Native versions, extras/markers, prereleases, required wheel/sdist set and partial upload |
| Cargo+napi | Selected target builds, owner-defined lifecycle hooks preserved, Callisto-owned publication ordering and clean install/load |
| Cargo+Maturin | Co-located static/dynamic metadata, native version mapping and wheel metadata |
| Mixed workspace | No unrelated addon builds, foreign-name rewrites or missed affected lockfiles |
| History/retry | Correct ownership through transitions; missing push/forge/assets/files completed with original artifacts |

Retain local real-registry tests and record missing prerequisites as skips. Run `just ci` for implementation handoffs and workflow contract/policy checks for workflow changes. Measure fresh-repo first publication against the owner's ten-minute goal. Go/NuGet examples check model assumptions only; they are not new runtime gates.

## Owner decisions

- Canonical-reference compatibility, including colon form; source-owner representation and versioned wire migration.
- Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only scope, npm channel policy, universal checksum requirements and wrapper bump severity.
- Inferred-only/manual releases: managed PR selection depends on changesets and verification requires a consumed changeset (ADR 2). Decide before broadening authorization.
- Build or drop a workspace-wide source-error-discard check; the Cargo lint is only a partial guard.
- Default tags for fixed/independent mode must be settled with canonical ownership, not a second tag-selection mechanism.
- Release-commit provenance: an unkeyed digest and decision/diff agreement do not prove which producer created the file. Decide whether existing authority is sufficient.
- Rust-cache pin in orin-dx/actions, bot-PR check policy and token rotation remain owner items.

## Other open work retained

- npm writes normalize arbitrary JSON layout; decide whether more than key order/indentation/line endings is needed.
- Preserve redacted stderr for indeterminate provider failures; never stream unredacted native-tool output.
- Publish final migration notices for retired callisto-format, callisto-vcs, callisto-conventional and callisto-changelog, naming callisto-model or callisto-graph.
- Evaluate rustc-provided target facts instead of the 18-triple table without making the core model Rust-target-specific.
- Require kind in explicit registry entries and attest napi .node outputs; define scope before adding a gate.
- Pin the floating moon minor in .prototools after checking proto compatibility.

## After 1.0 (additive)

- Effective-config explain from ConfigProvenance; remove redundant default-valued config afterward.
- .sha256 release-asset sidecars and proto verification.
- Glob fixed-group members.
- Auto-include README, LICENSE and CHANGELOG in release archives.
- Go/NuGet adapters and additional relationships only when concrete use cases and native tests justify them.

# REQ-DX-V1: world-class release DX and correctness for v1

Stakeholder: Callisto owner (sole maintainer); users releasing Rust, npm (incl. napi-rs) and Python monorepos.

Status: open. The command surface and release machinery exist, but verified correctness and integration gaps remain. [The findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md) records evidence and coverage; [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [sequencing plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json) track the work. Cargo real-registry tests now exist; they do not establish full production release-path coverage.

Why: Callisto's release engine is rigorous but its surface is confusing and its setup is heavy. Goal: a new repo goes from `callisto init` to its first published release in under 10 minutes, with one obvious release command and no known correctness bugs.

## Decided by the owner

- The main verb is `release`. Flow: `add` → `version` → `release`.
- `callisto release` publishes every package whose version has no release yet: registry publish, tag, forge release. `--dry-run` previews it on any branch.
- User-facing commands shown in `--help`: init, add, status, version, release, pre, snapshot, completions. Plumbing stays callable but hidden.
- `add` keeps both modes: interactive wizard on a TTY, flags for automation, clear error with the needed flags when neither.
- Breaking changes are fine pre-1.0; no external users.
- Current implementation scope is Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm (including napi-rs) and Python/PyPI. Keep architecture room for Go and C#/.NET/NuGet without implementing those adapters now.
- Prefer canonical ecosystem-qualified references and deliberate legacy migration over collision-triggered identity magic. Release ownership, native distribution identity, version authority and effects are separate responsibilities; the detailed proposal is [the scoped model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- Do not build a universal package manager, build scheduler, cross-language inference engine or persisted execution journal. Native tools/CI own compilation, packing and authentication.

## Done when

- `callisto --help` lists exactly the 8 user commands; each has one plain-language line.
- `callisto release --dry-run` with no flags prints the full plan on any branch; `callisto release` with no flags performs it locally with credentials in the environment.
- The CI split (plan → build → execute across jobs) works through `release` flags or hidden subcommands, and callisto's own workflow uses them.
- `publish`, `plan-publish`, `tag`, `filter-plan` are removed; one plan implementation serves preview and execution and includes every check listed above.
- Text output uses colour/tables on a TTY, plain text when piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, no schema versions in text; `status` shows cascaded bumps.
- Verified defects in the findings register are fixed with regression coverage across affected siblings. CI runs the shipped runtime behavior; no shipped Cargo feature variants. Existing real local npm/Cargo/PyPI tests are retained, with skipped prerequisites distinguished from executed coverage and production binding/observation paths checked separately.
- `callisto init` detects ecosystems/packages, asks only intent (fixed vs independent; release artifacts if binaries exist), writes minimal config, and can write a GitHub workflow using `callisto-action` of <= 40 lines; a non-interactive mode exists.

Scratch under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad/r2/redact/ (/usr/bin/git, plain commands, Write tool for scripts; GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null). A real binary exists at .../v1-research/target/debug/callisto.

CONTEXT: a prior pass claimed that `ProviderIndeterminateCause` (find it, probably in crates/callisto-model/src/release/) carries no details field, so when a provider (cargo/npm/twine/gh/git) fails ambiguously (native tool exits non-zero, network, auth) the operator sees only a coarse cause and not the tool's own (redacted) stderr. The owner has NOT decided the allow-list shape or the persisted wire change.

TASK: (1) Verify the current state precisely: every place native tool output is captured, truncated, redacted, logged, persisted in a receipt/observation, or dropped (providers under crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/, exec seam in callisto-model/src/exec.rs, redaction code: grep redact/secret/mask/scrub/token; how credentials/env are filtered; what the receipt and outcomes JSON contain; what the user sees on failure in text mode and json mode, and what the generated workflow logs shows). Reproduce a representative indeterminate failure with the real binary if feasible using fake tools on PATH (e.g. a fake `cargo` script that prints a token-like string and a multi-line error to stderr and exits 101; see crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/ tests for how they fake tools) via `callisto release --dry-run` is NOT sufficient since it does not execute; if you cannot reach execution without registry access, say so and rely on source + the test harness. (2) Enumerate design options for retaining redacted stderr: (R-a) in-memory only, printed once to the operator's stderr after redaction; (R-b) persisted in the receipt as a bounded redacted field (wire change to receipt v2 / ProviderIndeterminateCause); (R-c) allow-list of known-safe lines/patterns per tool vs deny-list redaction of secrets; (R-d) a pointer only (tool name, exit code, hash of output). For each: security risk (secrets that native tools echo: npm tokens in .npmrc errors, twine URLs with credentials, `gh` tokens, cargo registry tokens, URLs with userinfo, env dumps), what existing redaction covers (verify with tests, list file:line), wire/schema/digest impact (receipt is schemaVersion 2; ADR 3 no journal; wire-compat.md reader policy), cost, and fit with the AGENTS.md invariant that user-facing errors derive miette::Diagnostic with a code and a fix. Look at prior art briefly (cargo-dist, Terraform, GitHub Actions secret masking, npm's own log redaction) with URLs. (3) A recommendation with a concrete minimal design and file-level change list, tests (must fail on old behavior; include a secret-leak negative test), spec criteria to amend, PR slicing and S/M/L size. (4) Residual owner decisions as concrete either/or (e.g. persist vs print-only; bounded size; allow-list vs deny-list). (5) What you could not verify. Report max ~1400 words, evidence tagged [REPRODUCED]/[SOURCE file:line]/[WEB url].

  ### Table stakes Callisto lacks
  
  - Tokenless publishing on all three registries.
  - A documented bootstrap for the first publish.
  - Checksums for release assets.
  - PyPI attestations.
  - An init that reduces credential setup (release-plz stores secrets).
  - A stated SLSA level and verification recipe for consumers.
  - An `npm` pnpm-catalog story (Changesets lacks it too, so this is not table stakes).
  - cargo-semver-checks integration for library crates. This is a release-plz selling point, not universal.
  
  ### Differentiators: verified, with limits
  
  1. **Committed, digest-sealed decision verified against the merged diff** (ADR 2). The competitor docs I read describe no equivalent. release-please trusts a manifest of versions plus label state, which its own troubleshooting page calls fragile. I found no counter-example, but absence in docs is not proof of absence.
  2. **No-journal rerun adoption.** This is narrower than "unique". Changesets and release-plz already adopt by registry presence per package. Callisto's real extension is observing tag, draft, assets and registries together, failing closed on conflict, and writing a receipt (ADR 3). Roadmap tasks T08/T12 are required for this to hold. `docs/how-callisto-works.md` itself admits a tag does not yet prove every distribution published and that a fresh local retry can say "Nothing to release." That is the release-plz #2292 class, so it must be fixed before 1.0.
  3. **Credential isolation baked into generated workflows** (plan and build jobs get no secrets; script-enforced). Changesets only recommends splitting. This is a real differentiator. Do not weaken it when adding OIDC.
  4. **Cross-ecosystem dual outputs.** Knope already versions one package across several files. The differentiator is the publish DAG across Cargo, npm and PyPI with one tag and a shared owner. Do not claim "only tool with dual outputs".

State the SlugFest 48h expiry. |
  | 3 | The tag-is-not-completion gap (T08) | `docs/how-callisto-works.md` limits; [release-plz #2292](https://github.com/release-plz/release-plz/issues/2292) | M | Keep it a 1.0 blocker. It is the core claim. |
  | 4 | No PyPI attestations; PyPI path has no tokenless route | Section 2 | M | Decide between twine plus `--attestations` plus a mint step, or adopting `uv publish`. Prefer the tool that supports both; it affects ADR 4. |
  | 5 | No checksum sidecars | `ROAD-TO-V1.md` "After 1.0" | S | Move into 1.0. Cheap, expected, and `proto` can verify them. |
  | 6 | Immutable-release interaction untested and undocumented | `docs/releasing.md` recovery section | S | Add a recovery caveat. State "enable immutable releases after the first release", or test a release with it on. |
