  | 10 | No SLSA level stated; no SBOM | Section 2 | S (doc) | Say "L2 for binaries via attest-build-provenance". Mark SBOM out of scope for 1.0. |
  | 11 | No semver-checks for Rust libraries | release-plz | M | Defer. Recommend it as a CI step in docs. |
  
  ## 5. C(2). Adopt, avoid, document as out of scope
  
  Adopt:
  
  - Trusted publishing as the default in generated workflows, with token fallback for the first publish.
  - Pin the trusted publisher to the exact workflow filename. For crates.io and npm, `workflow_dispatch` recovery from the same file works. Do not use `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` for publishing (blocked by crates.io).
  - `.sha256` sidecars, and tell users to verify with `gh attestation verify`.
  - Keep the draft-then-publish release flow, so immutable releases work.
  
  Avoid:
  
  - A native crates.io client. It breaks ADR 4, and a token-exchange step does the job.
  - A GitHub Environment or reviewer gate (owner policy).
  - Putting any registry credential, including `id-token`, in plan or build jobs.
  - Claiming `--workspace` atomicity. Cargo itself says it is not atomic.
  - Claiming "only tool with X" for the differentiators above.
  
  Document as out of scope:
  
  - SBOM generation.
  - npm staged publishing.
  - Go and NuGet publishers.
  - Private-index OIDC.
  - Cross-registry atomic rollback (already stated).
  
  Users care because a 2026 reviewer will ask "where are your tokens?" first.
  
  ## 6. C(3). Examples worth copying
  
  - `release-plz init` stores secrets through `gh` in one interactive step ([docs](https://release-plz.dev/docs/usage/init)). Copy the shape: have `callisto init` print the exact trusted-publisher settings per registry (workflow filename, environment) instead of storing secrets.
  - Nx `--first-release` makes bootstrap an explicit mode ([docs](https://nx.dev/docs/guides/nx-release/publish-rust-crates)). Callisto could offer a named first-publish path.
  - release-plz quickstart gives one workflow block per auth mode ([quickstart](https://release-plz.dev/docs/github/quickstart)). `docs/publishing.md` could show OIDC first and token as fallback.
  - cargo-dist and GoReleaser each document one verification recipe for consumers ([GoReleaser](https://goreleaser.com/customization/publish/attestations/)). Callisto already has the verify command in `setup-callisto`. Publish it in the README.
  - maturin `generate-ci` emits trusted-publishing config as an option ([docs](https://www.maturin.rs/distribution.html)).
  - release-please's troubleshooting page documents the force-run label recovery ([docs](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md)). `docs/errors.md` already covers this shape; keep a short "stuck release" index.
  
  ## 7. What I could not verify
  
  - The crates.io trusted-publishing doc page does not render by fetch. Claims rest on the RFC, the Rust blog and release-plz docs. Whether a crates.io token is scoped to one crate or several is unverified.
  - Whether npm OIDC still works when the generated workflow's `.npmrc` interpolates an empty `NPM_TOKEN`.
  - Whether twine's GitHub OIDC path works without the PyPA action. Sources conflict.
  - Whether staged npm publishes confuse Callisto's `npm view` observation.
  - cargo-workspaces, Rust-lang's own release tooling, Knope publishing, Nx Python support and python-semantic-release monorepo support: not researched or not found.
  - Dates for the release-plz and Changesets pages (year or day not shown), and the cargo-release version conflict.
  - Whether `actions/attest-build-provenance@v4.2.2` is being superseded by `actions/attest@v4` (GitHub's doc now shows `actions/attest@v4`).
  - No hosted-run, timing or competitor-execution testing was done.

The competitor report is in, and I confirmed two of its claims in the repo:
- `.github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh` allows `id-token` only in the `build-artifact` job, and it has a self-test that fails if `execute` gets it. So crates.io trusted publishing would need an owner decision about that rule.

  T06 plan, verified against v0.11.0 (d1f0de357). Nothing built or edited; scratch repos are in `.../scratchpad/r2/t06/` (w1-w6, run1-5.sh).
  
  ## 1. Verified current state
  
  **What the plan got wrong**
  - `GroupTable::from_groups` no longer skips the conflict check [SOURCE config/groups.rs:263-291]. #192 added `try_from_groups` (shares `validate_membership`, 4 tests); `from_groups` is `#[deprecated]` and has zero callers. T06 step 4 is stale: delete it.
  - `PackageId::resolve_unique` is unused in production [SOURCE]. Its only callers are 4 tests under `#[allow(deprecated)]` at model/identity.rs:434-554.
  - `IdentityIndex::resolve_human`, `display_form` and the `bare` map are also dead in production [SOURCE]. `walk.rs` maintains `bare`, but only tests read it (graph/identity.rs:358, walk/tests.rs:644/800). `prefixed` is live, but only to derive `promoted_siblings` (lib.rs:130).
  
  **Surfaces the plan missed**
  - `GroupTable::resolve` hand-rolls its own `claimed_by` (config/groups.rs:157-196) instead of sharing `validate_membership`. [REPRODUCED] w2: `members = ["x-core","@x/core"]` names one dual-manifest owner twice and is silently accepted. `try_from_groups` would reject it as E250.
  - `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]` rules match `id.name()` only, not native names (`rule_applies` at config/resolve.rs:311, `matches_in_ecosystems` at config/pattern.rs:56, applied in walk.rs:620/626).
    - [REPRODUCED] w2: `match = "npm/@x/core"` on a Cargo+npm owner `x-core` is dropped, with only a warning "matched no packages". `cargo/x-*` applies, `npm/@x/*` does not.
    - A resolver-based rule match fixes this.
  - Init has its own string resolver: `InitFacts::product_package` (graph/commands/init.rs:118) accepts bare names, so `--product-package` is a parse site. `init` already emits qualified ids via `qualified_id` (init.rs:177), which is a second copy of the canonical-ref logic.
  - Colon is also emitted, not just parsed: identity.rs:486 (dependency-ambiguity diagnostic, pinned by WS-ID-07) and release.rs:199 (E227 detail says "`cargo:pkg`").
  - Changeset entries parse in three places: aggregate.rs:317, status.rs:40 and status.rs:203.
  - `Ecosystem::from_prefix` lowercases, so `CARGO/x-core` is accepted today [REPRODUCED w2 changeset].
  - Dead `ReleaseEntry.package: PackageId` in model/plan.rs:94 (no users).
  
  **Parse sites, with what they accept today and what changes**
  
  | Site | Today | Required change |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | model/identity.rs:60 `PackageId::parse` | bare, `eco:`, `eco/`, any case | reject known-prefix colon (E316); add `parse_canonical` (Prefixed only, lowercase) |
  | `IdentityIndex::resolve` / `resolve_id` (graph/identity.rs:312-340) | bare, `eco:`, `eco/`; E102/E103 | split into `resolve_ref` and `resolve_changeset_key` |
  | config/groups.rs:186 (`index.resolve`), platform lookup first at :174 | bare, colon, slash | canonical only; keep raw platform-manifest names native |
  | config/resolve.rs:161 `parse_qualified_package` (product-package, artifact) | qualifies, accepts colon [REPRODUCED w5] | colon -> E316 |
  | config/resolve.rs:594 `[[package]] match` | bare, colon | canonical only; resolve via index in `resolve_packages` |
  | config/pattern.rs:25 `[[package-set]]` | `:` tried first, then `/` | `eco/glob` only; match native names per ecosystem |
  | cli add.rs:35 | bare and colon (`cargo:foo:patch` works) [REPRODUCED w1] | canonical only |
  | cli release.rs:190 `parse_release_selection` | colon alias; bare rejected (E227) [REPRODUCED] | drop the colon alias; `ReleasePackageId` already rejects `:` |
  | matrix.rs:116 `resolve_selected_package` | bare or colon [REPRODUCED] | canonical only |
  | `init --product-package` | bare or qualified | canonical only |
  | aggregate.rs:317, status.rs:40/203 (changeset keys); lib.rs:324 (pre.json keys) | bare, colon, slash | keep native/bare and canonical; reject colon |
  
  **Sites that already conform**
  - Release wires (decision, intent, `ReleasePackageId`) are canonical-only.
  - `init` emission is canonical.
  - `Package.id`-keyed internals are unchanged.
  
  **`display_name()` plays two roles.**
  - Persistence-derived: the default tag stem (model/tag.rs:74), the pre.json key (lib.rs:294), the pre-cursor ref `refs/callisto/pre-cursor/{display_name}` (conventional/pre_cursor.rs:8), and the changeset entry name `add` writes (add.rs:40).
  - Emission: `PackageId::Serialize` is `display_name`, so reports show bare for unpromoted packages [REPRODUCED w1: `"package": "bar"`].
  - Per (C) it must stay for the first group. A `PackageId` cannot canonicalize itself, because a `Bare` id carries no ecosystem. Canonicalization therefore needs index or package context.
  
  ## 2. Design
  
  **Resolver API**
  - Model: `PackageId::parse` returns `ColonForm{raw, canonical}` (E316) and rejects uppercase prefixes. New `PackageId::parse_canonical`. `ReleasePackageId` stays strict for release wires. Do not use it for status or matrix emission, because its safety name check is stricter than discovery.
  - Graph `IdentityIndex`, replacing `resolve`, `resolve_id`, `resolve_human` and `identifies`:
    - `resolve_ref(&str)`: canonical only, exact `(eco, native name)` lookup. Used by config, groups, rules, product/artifact, `add`, `matrix`, `init`. A group member may instead be a raw platform-manifest native name (checked first, as today).
    - `resolve_changeset_key(&str)`: canonical or native bare (E103 if ambiguous). Used by the three changeset sites and pre.json keys. Colon is a hard E316, not today's warn-and-skip, which would silently drop a bump in `version`.
    - `canonical(&PackageId) -> PackageId::Prefixed{primary eco, primary native name}`. Build it in `IdentityAssigner`, including `promotion_rekey`.
    - `suggest(raw)`: fix-it candidates.
  - `GroupTable::resolve` validates through the shared `validate_membership`, which closes the alias-duplicate hole.
  
  **Canonical output without touching tags or changeset files**
  - Call `canonical()` at the three report builders: plan.rs:73 `to_report`, status.rs:121, snapshot.rs:55.
  - Also apply it to `Diagnostic.package`.
  - Matrix keys come from canonical ids (matrix.rs:498/504/536, via `MatrixPackageInput.id`).
  - Leave `display_name()` for tags, pre.json keys, pre-cursor refs and changeset entries. `add` keeps writing the native/display name, which preserves @changesets/cli interop (ADR 1).
  - Defer or track the human prose that uses `display_name()`: pr_body.rs (about 15 sites) and changelog/render.rs. Convert the selector-bearing errors (graph/error.rs:77-168).
  
  **Errors**
  - Codes are allocated sequentially across crates. E315 is the highest (model/vcs/mod.rs:37), so add E316 and E317 to docs/errors.md; a model test enforces the doc rows.
  - E316: "package reference `cargo:foo` uses the `ecosystem:name` form". Help: "Write `cargo/foo`." In config it also names the key, e.g. "`[[fixed-group]] workspace` members".
  - E317: "package reference `callisto-model` must name its ecosystem". Help: "Write `cargo/callisto-model`", or list the candidates when ambiguous.
  
  **Unpromoted bare reference in config**
  - Error with a fix-it. Do not accept it.
  - Dogfood edits:
    - callisto.toml: 5 bare group members -> `cargo/callisto-*`.
    - AGENTS.md:24: `callisto-cli:<bump>` -> `cargo/callisto-cli:<bump>`.
    - docs/config.md:108-123 and :142.
    - docs/architecture/identity.md.
    - docs/errors.md (E227, E214 help).
    - ADR 12 text: it claims to revise the default-tag coupling, which (C) rejects. ADR 12 is still Proposed, so edit it.
  - `.changeset/*.md` stay valid (native names).
  - The `[[package]] match` and release entries in callisto.toml are already canonical.
  
  **Report and matrix fields that carry a package id**
  - `VersionReport.bumps[].package` and `bumps[].reason.via` (the Cascade and PeerEscalation variants).
  - `SnapshotReport.bumps[]`, same fields.
  - `StatusReport.packages[].package`.
  - `diagnostics[].package` in every report.
  - `MatrixReport` `platformTargets` and `runtimeVersions` keys.
  
  Not affected: Add, Pre, Init, and the release wires.
  
  **`schemaVersion`**
  - `SCHEMA_VERSION` is one global constant `= 1` (report.rs:9), and the value semantics change for unpromoted packages.
  - Recommendation: bump only status, version, snapshot and matrix to 2. The CHANGELOG (:239) documents bare keys as contract.
  - Matrix test MX-OUT-03 pins `{"schemaVersion":1,...}` exactly.
  
  **Shell and jq consumers**
  - No in-repo consumer reads the changing keys or fields.
  - templates/matrix_workflow.tmpl:70-73 feeds `.operations[].id.package` (already `ReleasePackageId`) to `matrix --package`, then reads `.platformTargets[]` values only. Its jq `add` merge of per-package maps is safe because canonical keys never collide.
  - The action scripts read `hasChangesets` and the receipt.
  - The pinned `.snap` is unaffected.
  
  ## 3. Test plan
  
  **New tests (each fails on old behavior)**
  - Colon is rejected with E316 naming the slash form, in:
    - group member
    - `[[package]]`
    - `[[package-set]]`
    - `product-package`
    - artifact package
    - `add`
    - `matrix`
    - `release`
    - a changeset key
    - a pre.json key
    - Old: all accepted.
  - Bare is rejected with E317 in config groups and rules and in the CLI args. A promoted bare group member must give E317, not E103. A raw platform name is still accepted. Old: accepted.
  - `[[package]] npm/@x/core` on a dual-manifest owner applies, and `npm/@x/*` applies. Old: dropped.
  - Group alias duplicate gives E250. Old: accepted.
  - `CARGO/x` is rejected.
  - Report and matrix keys are `cargo/foo` for an unpromoted package, and the tag is still `foo@…`.
  - Diagnostic ids are canonical.

  - **Mechanism:** `RegistryVersion{checksum: None}` for cargo and npm (`registry.rs:432-447,466-479`). ADR 3 adopts any exact version.
  - **Scenario:** someone manually publishes 1.0.1 from a dev machine. The release PR merges. Callisto skips the publish and writes `alreadySatisfied`. The tag exists only because no other tag is there to conflict (finding 1, scenario A).
  - **Plan coverage:** universal checksums are an open owner decision. The cross-source case combined with finding 1 is not noted.
  
  ### 6. Medium: trust boundary inside the credentialed `execute` job
  - **Persisted token [SOURCE]:** the job keeps checkout credentials with `contents: write` (`matrix_workflow.tmpl:223`, the zizmor ignore) and `id-token: write`. `cargo publish` verify builds and npm lifecycle scripts run inside it. They can read `.git/config` and the `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_*` variables. The CLI runner scrubs only a fixed credential list and not these (`runner.rs:14-27`, `credentials_needed_by`).
  - **Unsealed provenance [SOURCE]:** the Python "seal" is computed in the execute job over whatever files were downloaded (`matrix_workflow.tmpl`, "Write the artifact manifest"). Wheels have no provenance, unlike binary assets, which require attestation verification.

Cargo publishes with `--registry <key>` and `cargo info` runs from the workspace dir, and a `.npmrc` or `.cargo/config.toml` in the repo can route elsewhere.

  - **State is lost [SOURCE]:** state is in-memory (ADR 3), `execute_release` returns Err and drops it, and the only per-op stderr line is "already published".
  - **No read-only path [SOURCE]:** there is no read-only "what landed?" command. `release --dry-run` prints plan ops, not observations, and `release execute` rejects `--dry-run`.
  - **Unhelpful errors [REPRODUCED]:**
    - A cargo publish that dies after the upload landed reports E163 "Resolve the underlying registry condition and retry".

  - **No ceiling [REPRODUCED]:** with tag `libx@1.5.0` present and the manifest at 0.1.1, `version` plans 0.1.2 and `release --dry-run` plans publishing 0.1.1. The base is the manifest only (`lib.rs:210`).
  - **Dist-tags [SOURCE]:** every prerelease publishes with npm tag `next` (`derive.rs:397-399`), snapshots included. A stable backport publishes with no tag, so it moves `latest` backwards. Owner decision open.
  
  ### 9. Low-Medium: smaller items
  - **Build-dependency selection [REPRODUCED plan]:** `release --package cargo/a` is accepted although `a` has a Cargo build-dependency on an unreleased workspace crate. `require_dependencies_selected` checks only runtime, optional and peer edges (`derive.rs:772`).
  - **Per-operation trust recheck [SOURCE]:** the executor runs `recheck_trust` before every operation (`release_execution.rs:39`). That is about six git calls including `git status --untracked-files=all`, which is slow on large repos. A publish hook that leaves untracked, non-ignored files aborts the release mid-run.
  - **Adoption hazard [REPRODUCED plan]:** with no config, `release --dry-run` plans every publishable manifest at its current version. The workflow's first push would publish all of them.
  - **Snapshot has no publish path [REPRODUCED]:** `snapshot` leaves a dirty tree, and `release` then refuses with E267.
  - **Concurrent draft releases [SOURCE, unverified on GitHub]:** two concurrent runs could create two drafts for one tag, and lookup is by tag via GraphQL.
  - **Manifest-write surprises:**
    - `version.workspace = true` is rewritten to a literal version in the member. The docs say manifest diffs show only version changes.
    - `callisto version` creates and stages a new `Cargo.lock` when none was tracked and it is not ignored [REPRODUCED].
  - **Stale comment:** the `TagTemplate::default_for` doc comment contradicts ADR 11 (`tag.rs:71`).
  - **Tag signing:** tags are always `--no-sign`.
  
  ## Lenses with no flaw found
  - **E124 re-derivation, intent digest and run envelope:** sound. Intent derivation is fail-closed, and the envelope cross-checks source, digest and orchestration revision.
  - **Registry or intent tampering:** I found no way to retarget an effect without the intent's source commit binding it. The digest covers a manifest-bytes fingerprint, the tag template, targets and the remote.
  - **Tag adoption (ADR 9):** consistent between local and remote.
  - **Yanked versions:** fail closed.
  - **Promotion and tag history:** the ownership fallback worked on a promotion probe.
  
  ## Design strengths worth keeping
  - Proof-token state machine (`AbsentProof` and `ExactEvidence`), with a single `transition()` mutator.
  - Operation DAG sealed by digest, re-derived at execute, and the fault-injection simulator.
  - Draft, then upload, then publish ordering for forge releases.
  - Managed route verification of the release commit: it rejects unclaimed version changes and manifest/decision disagreement.
  - `ApplyPermit` plus `atomic_write` (mode-preserving, parent fsync).
  - Per-tool credential scrubbing, and a credential-free Python build job.
  - Read-only observation retries only, with effects never retried.
  
  ## Not verified
  - Real registry or GitHub behaviour: all effects used fakes.
  - JS changesets' pre-mode semantics.
  - Whether twine supports OIDC.

content.text:
The agent findings that matter most hold up: I reproduced or read nearly all of them myself, with no agents. Two came out softer than the agents reported, and a set of agent-only claims remains unvalidated.

**Reproduced on the real binary** (details in the "Validation pass" section of `.claude/plans/V1-REVIEW-2026-10-20.md`):
- **Lost publish after a rename (A1).** The bare-tag adoption reproduces. After the npm rename, only `npm/bar` is planned and the Cargo `foo` is silently dropped.
- **Wrong-commit tag (A2).** After a crash following publish at commit A and an unrelated commit B, `release` tags B. I used a fake `cargo` and a local bare remote.
- **Foreign version adopted (A5).** An already-published version is skipped and HEAD is tagged. Adopting an existing exact version is by design (ADR 3), so the defect is the tag target.
- **Pre-release mode (A3).** On the managed route it fails with E165, and `version` keeps bumping beta.0, beta.1, beta.2.
- **Dependency ranges (A4).**
  - A stale `^2.0.0-next.0` survives a pre-release cycle.
  - A Cargo compound range half-applies the tree, then fails with E208, and a rerun gives E121.
  - Poetry carets are not rewritten.
  - `>=0.1.0,<0.2` becomes `>=0.2.0, <1`.
- **Token and error text (A7).** A `Bearer` token prints in cleartext. E176 shows a Rust Debug dump and no tool text.
- **Dual packages and release graph (A8).**
  - `--package npm/dual` plans only the npm side.
  - A dependent waits on every publish of its dependency.
  - The product's forge publish waits only on the draft and uploads, not on a plugin's publish (read in `derive.rs:737-738`).
- **Spec drift.** Dirty worktree is E267 and shallow clone is E266, but the specs say E051. E049 exists only in the spec. Matrix JSON does have a `command` key. `version` creates and stages `Cargo.lock` when none is tracked.
- **Read from files.**
  - Crates inherit only `edition` and `repository`.
  - There is no semver-check, MSRV or scheduled job.
  - There are 2 fuzz targets.
  - `unwrap_used` and `expect_used` are set to allow.
  - `AGPL-3.0-only` is allowed.
  - ADRs 9 and 10 are still Proposed.
  - Three `how-callisto-works.md` limits are stale.
  - The simple workflow has no concurrency group.
  - The policy script allows `id-token` only in the build job.
  - The real-registry tests skip silently.

**Corrections to what the agents or I said earlier**
- **A6, snapshots.** The plan lists a publish and tag, but a real `release` refuses the dirty tree (E267) unless the snapshot is committed. Lower severity than first written.
- **A12, unknown changeset entries.** Leaving the file on disk is what the spec requires. The real defects are the missing unknown-package warning and the repeat bump.
- **A2 and A5.** These ran against a fake `cargo`. The behavior is consistent with the source, but I haven't run it against a real registry.

**Not validated by me** (agent evidence only):
- The concurrent-run scenario that leaves E167 permanently failing.
- A11, A13 and the Python dev-table skipping.
- Every count (public items, unwraps, 259 error codes, the 14% drift rate).
- Competitor and web claims, including trusted publishing, SlugFest and immutable releases.
- The install script's platform gaps.
- Any hosted GitHub behavior.
- The local TLS registry runs.
- Cargo through a local registry.

Say which of these you want checked next, or pick the first repair to start.

---
name: feedback-use-gh-stack
description: Stacked PRs in callisto must be GitHub-native stacks via `gh stack` (link/submit), not plain PRs with chained bases
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Create stacked PRs with `gh stack` (e.g. `gh stack link --base main b1 b2 ...`, or `gh stack link <stack#> <branch>` to grow). GitHub runs CI for every PR in a native stack; plain PRs whose base is another branch get no CI.

**Why:** 2026-09-26 I opened #160-163 as plain chained PRs; none got CI and I wrongly blamed the workflow's `branches: [main]` filter. The owner's stacks (#127, #159) are native stacks. A stack whose bottom base branch merged cannot retarget: unstack, `gh pr edit <n> --base main`, relink; a base change alone does not trigger CI (close/reopen did).

**How to apply:** When stacking, check `gh api repos/orin-dx/callisto/pulls/<n> -q .stack`. After a merge, restack onto main and relink. See [[feedback-verify-before-recommending]].
---
name: worktree-guard-command-shapes
description: "In a worktree-isolated session the bash guard refuses compound commands, heredocs and any text mentioning git; use /usr/bin/git, plain commands, and scripts written with the Write tool."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c
  modified: 2026-10-18T04:26:47.634Z
---

In a worktree-isolated session the shell guard refuses commands it cannot prove stay inside the worktree: heredocs, loops with computed arguments, `python3 - <<EOF` whose text mentions git, `cd` plus several git calls, and a leading `git` that rtk rewrites.

**Why:** the guard reads any command text that names git and refuses when it cannot verify the target worktree. It cost many retries across the nested-workspace stack (#241 to #247).

**How to apply:**
- Call git as `/usr/bin/git`, one plain command at a time, from the worktree directory.
- Put multi-step logic and Python edits in a script written with the Write tool under the scratchpad, then run it as `python3 -I script.py` or `bash script.sh`.
- Avoid the word git inside inline Python or shell text. Write the script to a file instead.

result.output:
When two or more directories declare the same name and no ecosystem declares it in more than one of them, each package is promoted to an ecosystem-qualified id, displayed as `cargo/foo`. Promotion preserves the package's key (its workspace-relative directory) and CHANGELOG path; `cargo/foo` selects it in both states. Newly created default tags use `{display id}@{version}`, so promotion changes their namespace. A promoted package's last tag is also found among `foo@*` tags whose commit contains its manifest and no other same-named package's. A bare `pre.json` `initialVersions` key moves to the one same-named package that existed when `pre.json` was added, else `version` fails with E245.
A Cargo package inherits from the Cargo workspace that governs it, found the way Cargo finds it (`cargo::enclosing_workspace_manifest`): `package.workspace`, else the nearest manifest at or above the package with a `workspace` table, never above the workspace root. That workspace can be below the root, so the walk, the version guard, release-commit verification, lockfile refresh and `registry_argv` all resolve it per package. Cargo does not judge membership for inheritance, and neither does this lookup: a root that excludes or omits the package is a repository Cargo itself rejects.

`Workspace::load` returns only a complete workspace, and it is the only way to get one. Every manifest the walk cannot open (for its platform role, publish targets or dependencies) is recorded as an error-level `ManifestUnresolved` diagnostic, and `load` turns any of them into E313 naming each manifest once, so no command sees a roster smaller than the repository.

For a promoted package, `TagIndex::build` also considers bare-name tags. `history::sole_owner_at` picks the same-named candidate whose first canonical manifest path exists at the tag's commit. When none does, because the directory moved or the package gained a higher-priority manifest, it asks which ecosystems had a manifest declaring the shared name at that commit, found with `git grep` and confirmed by reading only the matching manifests. The owner is the one candidate whose own manifest in such an ecosystem has that native name today, taken from the identity index. Two or more matches, or none, mean no owner. `assign_promoted_pre_keys` applies the same check at the commit that added `pre.json`, and E245 reports a baseline with no unique owner.

A demoted package, whose same-named sibling was removed, also considers the qualified tags of its first manifest's ecosystem and keeps the newest version across both families.

A rename that changes the native name, or a move that changes it too, leaves no evidence in Git. Declare it with `previous-tag-templates`; do not infer it from the directory key.

A package that did not make a `{name}@{version}` tag no longer takes it as its last release, and a version whose only tag is another package's is no longer skipped as already released.

- `TagIndex::build` now takes a bare package's newest default-template tag only if the tag's commit did not hold the name in another ecosystem, using the same history check as the promoted case. A rejected tag is dropped, the next newest is tried, and the rejection is reported as a `tag-owned-by-another-package` info diagnostic that points to `previous-tag-templates`.

- A commit with no manifest under the name, or history that cannot be read, is no evidence of another owner, so the tag is taken as before. That keeps shallow clones and hand-made tags working. I chose this over refusing in that case; say if you want the strict rule.
- Cost: one manifest read per bare package with a tag in the common case, and a roster lookup only when that read does not match.

Tests: three scenarios (renamed owner, removed owner, tag of a different package at the same version) fail without the gate, plus a test that a package keeps its own tags. The release workflow `callisto init` generates for a simple workspace now runs one release at a time.

- The simple template had no `concurrency` group, while the matrix template and Callisto's own release workflow do. Two pushes to the default branch in a row started two `release` jobs. Each releases whatever is untagged at its own HEAD, so the second could tag a commit whose bytes the first had already published, and the loser of the tag push failed with "reference already exists", which a rerun at the same commit then could not recover.
- The `release` job now has `concurrency: {group: callisto-release, cancel-in-progress: false}`: a running release is never cancelled, and a queued one runs against the newer HEAD, which contains the earlier release commit. The `version-pr` job is left unserialized.
- The trigger moved to the one-line flow form (`on: {push: {branches: [...]}}`) so the workflow with all three ecosystems stays at 39 lines, within the 40-line goal that `render_workflow_wires_a_secret_per_detected_ecosystem` enforces. Semantics are unchanged.

This does not change which commit a local `release` tags when it adopts an already-published version; that is a separate decision. The pinned simple-workflow snapshot and CLI-WF-03 are updated. `just ci` passes.
EOF

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ## Stack mechanics

Use Git worktrees and native GitHub stacks.

- Create only authorized branches/worktrees from a committed, recorded baseline. Each worker gets a named parent revision, task packet and exclusive write set. Do not branch agents from a dirty shared checkout.
- Stacked PRs are native GitHub stacks (`gh stack link <PRs bottom to top>`); plain chained PRs targeting a parent branch get no CI because `.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml` triggers only for PRs targeting `main`. Each PR must pass `just ci` on its own.
- Review the child delta with `rtk proxy git diff <parent>...<child>`. Also inspect the complete `main`-to-child diff and run tests on the combined stack. A passing parent is not verification of its child.
- Merge parent first. Save its reviewed tip before merge; after a squash/rebase merge, replay only child commits onto updated main, using the recorded parent tip as the exclusion boundary (for example `rtk proxy git rebase --onto origin/main <recorded-parent-tip> <child-branch>`). Inspect the resulting parent-only/full diff and rerun applicable checks before merging the child. Do not assume GitHub removes ancestor commits automatically. A required force push needs explicit approval and uses `--force-with-lease`.
- Keep stacks shallow: normally two or three open dependent PRs. Merge a verified compilation boundary before extending the next model layer; do not accumulate the full architecture as one speculative stack.
- Independent lanes are sibling PRs, not artificial ancestry. Shared-interface changes land in their common parent before parallel descendants implement adapters/fixtures against those fixed interfaces.
- Each PR includes its own regression and current spec/doc amendment. Use one changeset per independent consumer-facing topic; do not add a changeset just for internal planning or duplicate a parent's changeset in a child delta.
- Commit/PR actions remain coordinator-owned and owner-approved. Workers never push, merge, approve CI, edit release policy or publish versions.

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrite

- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

The exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve t

ROOT = "/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/stack-d01/"


def sub(path, old, new, count=1):

    s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()

    open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(old, new))


# ---- ADR 12
adr = "docs/adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md"
sub(adr, "This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.",
    "This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision, including its default tag; it is not superseded by this documentation change.")
text = open(ROOT + adr, encoding="utf-8").read()
start = text.index("## Proposed decision")
end = text.index("## Options considered")
decision = """## Proposed decision

- Require canonical slash-qualified distribution references (`cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name`, `pypi/name`) in `callisto.toml` (groups, package rules, product and artifact packages), in report and matrix keys, and in command-line arguments. Reject the colon form everywhere. A `pypi/` reference uses the declared name. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names and resolve them when read. A changeset entry names the owner package, not a distribution, and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli` (ADR 1).
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Release ownership is derived, not stored: the owner of a package's shared tag, forge release and announcement is its first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI. The intent digest seals it and `release execute` re-derives it, so no owner field or wire change is needed for the current scope.
- Keep ADR 11's default tag, `{display id}@{version}`, and never rename existing tags. A package takes only the tags its commit shows it made, and `previous-tag-templates` declares a rename.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner: selecting one distribution of a package releases all of them, a product's announcement waits for the tag of each package whose asset it carries, and a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.
- Co-located Cargo and Maturin, whose Python version is derived from Cargo, is after v1.

Channel and private-registry policies are not decided here and are not release gates.

"""
open(ROOT + adr, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text[:start] + decision + text[end:])

# ---- V1-IMPLEMENTATION: replace the D01 section
impl = "docs/projects/V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md"
text = open(ROOT + impl, encoding="utf-8").read()
start = text.index("## D01: approved directions and remaining model choices")
end = text.index("## Stack mechanics")
d01 = """## D01: decided contracts

The owner approved Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as current scope, architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet, registry publication before shared tags and public announcements, and package-owner control of native lifecycle hooks. The remaining contracts were decided on 2026-10-20; [ADR 12](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) records them and stays proposed until the canonical-reference work lands.

| Contract | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical references | Required in `callisto.toml`, report and matrix keys and command-line arguments; the colon form is rejected everywhere. Changesets and `pre.json` keep native names and resolve them when read, so `@changesets/cli` interoperability and dual-manifest owners keep working. Whether the status, version, snapshot and matrix reports bump their `schemaVersion` is decided with T06 |
| Owner identity | Derived: the first release id of the package by ecosystem priority Cargo, npm, PyPI, sealed by the intent digest and re-derived at execute. No owner field and no opaque ID |
| Tags | The default stays `{display id}@{version}`; existing tags are never renamed; a native rename is declared with `previous-tag-templates` |
| Wire compatibility | No change for the current scope: release documents are already canonical-only and strict, and an intent from an older version is re-planned, never rerun across versions |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases | A legacy and a canonical key with different versions fail with E305 |
| Maturin | After v1 |

Registry file set, Python destinations, announcement ordering, dual-package selection and lifecycle hooks are decided and implemented. Area specs stay current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch.

"""
open(ROOT + impl, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text[:start] + d01 + text[end:])
sub(impl, "## Architectural stack after D01", "## Architectural stack")

# ---- ROAD-TO-V1
road = "docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md"
text = open(ROOT + road, encoding="utf-8").read()
sub(road, ", including the D01 owner-contract checkpoint", "")
lines = [l for l in text.split("\n") if not l.startswith("- D01:")]
open(ROOT + road, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines))
sub(road, "do not treat architectural packets as fully gated implementer handoffs before D01.", "the D01 contracts are decided in ADR 12.")

# ---- plan JSON
p = ROOT + "docs/projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json"
d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
d["tasks"] = [t for t in d["tasks"] if t["id"] != "D01"]

    if t["id"] == "T06":
        t["steps"] = [
            "Baseline: IdentityIndex.resolve_id resolves native names; the status helpers no longer use PackageId::resolve_unique, which is unused outside its tests. Changesets and pre.json keep native names resolved at read time, with a hard error for colon. Platform-manifest npm names in groups stay native. Do not change tag names.",
            "Match [[package]] and [[package-set]] rules through the identity index so a dual-manifest owner's secondary native name applies. Share group membership validation between GroupTable::resolve and try_from_groups, and delete the dead from_groups, resolve_unique and resolve_human with a Breaking note.",
            "Emit canonical ids from one function in the report builders, matrix keys and diagnostics, leaving display_name() for tags, pre.json keys and changeset entries. Decide the schemaVersion of the status, version, snapshot and matrix reports with this task.",
            "Add paired status/version/matrix/release-selector tests for non-primary native names, scoped npm names, declared Python names, duplicate native distribution IDs, rejected colon and bare references, and deterministic report ordering. Retain glob patterns as a separate language.",
            "Slice into reviewable PRs: delete dead code and share group validation; reject the colon form; canonical-required config and rules, with the dogfood callisto.toml and AGENTS.md; canonical CLI arguments; canonical emission and the report version. Run rtk cargo test -p callisto-model, rtk cargo test -p callisto-graph and rtk cargo test -p callisto-cli sequentially."
        ]
        crit = t.get("covers_criteria", [])
        for c in ["WS-ID-07", "WS-CFG-03", "WS-CFG-04", "WS-CFG-08", "VER-PRE-01", "CLI-ADD-06", "REL-CMD-07"]:
            if c not in crit:
                crit.append(c)
        t["covers_criteria"] = crit
for b in d["batches"]:
    b["task_ids"] = [x for x in b["task_ids"] if x != "D01"]
d["batches"] = [b for b in d["batches"] if b["task_ids"]]
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(d, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

- **#255:** `--package` on one identity of a dual package releases the whole package.

The redaction stack:

- **#261:** missing real-registry tools fail instead of skipping under CI. Its first hosted run failed because the coverage job doesn't install those tools. That confirmed the skips had been silent, and I made the coverage job opt out.

**Standalone PRs**

- **#263:** crate metadata and package trimming. `cargo package` still builds all four crates.
- **#264:** the simple workflow serializes releases. I moved its trigger to one line to stay within the 40-line goal.

- **Stack depth:** the release stack is 5 deep, against the repo guideline of 2 or 3.

#!/bin/bash
# Re-sign every commit on the PR branches, preserving trees. Writes new tips to $OUT; does not push.
set -euo pipefail
G=/usr/bin/git
REPO=/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-callisto/15c732d1-457b-4efc-91e5-664943f21b1c/scratchpad
WT=$S/resign
OUT=$S/resign_tips.txt
cd "$REPO"
$G fetch -q origin
$G worktree remove --force "$WT" 2>/dev/null || true
$G worktree add -q --detach "$WT" origin/main
: > "$OUT"

# "branch parent" ; parent "-" means a root whose parent commit is kept as is
CHAIN="
docs/maturin-post-v1 -
docs/record-d01-decisions docs/maturin-post-v1
fix/tag-ownership-by-name -
fix/bare-tag-ownership fix/tag-ownership-by-name
fix/expand-dual-package-selection fix/bare-tag-ownership
fix/product-waits-for-plugin-owner fix/expand-dual-package-selection
fix/dependency-edge-publish-granularity fix/product-waits-for-plugin-owner
fix/redact-shaped-secrets -
fix/redact-failed-command-output fix/redact-shaped-secrets
test/real-registry-tests-fail-in-ci fix/redact-failed-command-output
docs/correct-stale-statements -
chore/crate-metadata-and-deps -
fix/simple-workflow-serializes-releases -
fix/poetry-caret-rewrite -
fix/group-duplicate-by-alias -
fix/version-warns-about-unknown-changeset-entries -
"
declare -A OLDTIP NEWTIP
echo "$CHAIN" | while read -r br parent; do
  [ -z "${br:-}" ] && continue
  echo "$br $($G rev-parse "origin/$br")"
done > "$S/resign_old.txt"
while read -r br sha; do OLDTIP[$br]=$sha; done < "$S/resign_old.txt"

echo "$CHAIN" | while read -r br parent; do :; done
while read -r br parent; do
  [ -z "${br:-}" ] && continue
  old=${OLDTIP[$br]}
  if [ "$parent" = "-" ]; then
    first=$($G rev-list --reverse "origin/main..$old" | head -1)
    base=$($G rev-parse "$first^")
    commits=$($G rev-list --reverse "origin/main..$old")
  else
    base=${NEWTIP[$parent]}
    commits=$($G rev-list --reverse "${OLDTIP[$parent]}..$old")
  fi
  $G -C "$WT" checkout -q --detach "$base"
  for c in $commits; do $G -C "$WT" cherry-pick -S --allow-empty "$c" >/dev/null; done
  new=$($G -C "$WT" rev-parse HEAD)
  [ "$($G rev-parse "$new^{tree}")" = "$($G rev-parse "$old^{tree}")" ] || { echo "TREE MISMATCH $br"; exit 1; }
  NEWTIP[$br]=$new
  echo "$br $old $new" >> "$OUT"
done < <(echo "$CHAIN")
echo done

- `parse` treats text before the first `:` or `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare.
- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
- `PackageId` is the display and selector form; `Package::key()` is the workspace-relative directory of the first canonical manifest. It survives display promotion, not a directory move. `ReleasePackageId` names each canonical distribution as `ecosystem/name` using that manifest's own native name.
- Default tags use `display_name()`: `foo@{version}` while bare, `cargo/foo@{version}` after promotion. Promotion therefore also changes the namespace of newly created default tags (ADR 11).
- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
  - Different names never match.
  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
- A dual-manifest package can have different native names. `IdentityIndex` resolves each ecosystem/name to its owner; the weak `matches` relation alone does not establish distribution identity or ownership.

## Resolving ambiguity

A workspace can hold `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens. Qualified selectors work before and after promotion. Canonical-only new references are planned in [the v1 design](polyglot-v1.md), not implemented by today's parser.

- `aggregate::resolve_target_package` resolves changeset entries through `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`, which maps qualified native distribution names to their owner and rejects ambiguous bare names. `status` attributes changeset entries and checks their well-formedness through the same resolver. `PackageId::resolve_unique` scans display ids, is deprecated, and is not equivalent for dual-manifest packages with different native names.

Add x86_64-apple and aarch64-linux; Windows is documented unsupported until it has CI. Drop the "under 10 minutes" number from user copy until T12-DX measures it | Claiming Windows without CI is worse than not claiming it | Yes |

| A6 snapshots | See decision 4 |

## Suggested order

1. Decide the one-way doors now: 5, 7, and the E317 go-ahead.
2. Start without further decisions: CI hygiene PR (MSRV, scheduled `cargo deny`, Cargo dependabot, semver-checks), generated-workflow `concurrency:`, pre-mode no-op fix, pre-write range hard stop.
3. T06 PRs 3 to 5 once 7 is confirmed.
4. A2 spike, then T08, then T12 with the local script.

Callisto is the one with a fixed group today: all five crates move together.

Independent versions suit michi because its crates are real libraries that people depend on separately. Callisto's libraries are the internals of one CLI, so lockstep is also a legitimate choice there.

| Lockstep | All five crates go to 1.0 together | Every release bumps every crate, and the 1.0 label on the libraries needs an "internal, no API guarantee" note |

I'm going with independent versions unless you say otherwise.

content.text:
Lockstep it is for callisto. It already is lockstep, so the plan only changes in one place.

The michi branch `refactor/michi-core-merge` fits what you said. Its `main` just hasn't caught up yet, which is why the repo still looked independent when I checked.

**Callisto's current state:**
- **Versioning:** all five crates are already in one fixed group in `callisto.toml`, so they already version in lockstep.
- **Crate count:** the consolidation to four published crates already shipped in #157. The four are `callisto-model`, `callisto-manifests`, `callisto-graph` and `callisto-cli`. The fifth, `callisto-fixtures`, is dev-only. The old `docs/crate-consolidation-plan` branch is stale, so I'll delete it.
- **Further merging:** `callisto-model` has to stay a separate crate because it is MIT and the others are FSL. Merging `callisto-manifests` into `callisto-graph` is possible, but I'd leave it for after 1.0. It doesn't affect the 1.0 contract.

**What changes in the plan:** decision 2 becomes "all four published crates go to 1.0 together." The libraries get an "internal implementation, no API stability guarantee" note, so a library change doesn't force a CLI major version. `cargo-semver-checks` then applies only to what we choose to promise. I'd start with `callisto-cli`'s `schema` output and its config and report formats, not the `pub` Rust items. That also drops the "split the libraries out of the fixed group" step, because no split is needed.

I'll update the plan notes and then start the CI hygiene PR.

# Local actions are commit-bound by the checkout. Every external GitHub action
# must use its full immutable commit hash; Docker actions must use an immutable
# content digest.
set -euo pipefail

status=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  reference=${line#*uses: }
  reference=${reference%% #*}
  reference=${reference//[[:space:]]/}
  # Workspace-relative and GitHub's self-repository references are bound to
  # local repository content; only external actions need an explicit pin.
  [[ "$reference" == ./* || "$reference" == '$/'* ]] && continue

  else
    valid='^[^@[:space:]]+@[0-9a-f]{40}$'

      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked

300	/// `PackageId::matches` alone is not enough here: it treats a Bare id as an

302	/// would otherwise match a same-named package that only exists in another
303	/// (a Cargo-only `foo`) -- `package_ecosystems` is the package's real,
304	/// manifest-derived ecosystem set, independent of whether its `PackageId`
305	/// happens to be Bare (unpromoted) or Prefixed.
306	pub(crate) fn rule_applies(rule_id: &PackageId, id: &PackageId, package_ecosystems: &[Ecosystem]) -> bool {
307	    if rule_id.name() != id.name() {
308	        return false;
309	    }
310	    match rule_id.ecosystem() {
311	        None => true,
312	        Some(eco) => package_ecosystems.contains(&eco),

319	/// first entry where `rule_id.ecosystem().is_some()` AND
320	/// [`rule_applies`] -- prefixed rules (`cargo/`, `npm/`, `pypi/`) always beat

337	        .packages

import re, sys

# usage: deltests.py file name [name...]; removes `#[test] fn name` (with preceding doc comments) up to its closing brace
path = sys.argv[1]
names = sys.argv[2:]
s = open(path).read()
for name in names:
    m = re.search(r'((?:^[ \t]*///[^\n]*\n)*)^([ \t]*)#\[test\]\n[ \t]*fn ' + re.escape(name) + r'\b', s, re.M)
    if not m:
        print('NOT FOUND', name)
        continue
    indent = m.group(2)
    start = m.start()

## `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]`

Both blocks share five override fields, parsed identically; `[[package]]` also accepts `previous-tag-templates`. `[[package]]`'s `match` is an exact `PackageId` (first matching rule wins, prefixed forms like `cargo/foo` take priority over bare `foo` regardless of declaration order). `[[package-set]]`'s `match` is a glob `PackagePattern` and can match many packages at once; `[[package]]` always takes priority over `[[package-set]]` for a given package.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `match` | string | required | `[[package]]`: exact ecosystem-qualified id or bare name. `[[package-set]]`: glob pattern. |
| `release-trigger` | string (`"changeset"` \| `"auto"`) | none — every field here is an `Option`; omitted means "use this package's own default", not a config-level default | What causes this package to be considered for release |
| `publish-to` | array of strings (`"crates-io"` \| `"npm"` \| `"pypi"` \| `"nuget"` \| `"github-release"` \| `"none"`) | none | Where this package publishes |
| `tag-template` | string | none | Git tag template, e.g. `"callisto@{version}"` |
| `previous-tag-templates` | array of strings | `[]` | `[[package]]` only (`[[package-set]]` rejects it). Earlier tag templates checked (in order) for this package's last release tag, only if `tag-template` finds none. They are matched by name only, so this is how a renamed package claims the tags it made under its old name |
| `changelog` | string | none | Changelog path, relative to the package's own root. Forward-slash-separated only; rejected if absolute or containing `..` (E113). |
| `pre-major-inference` | string (`"off"` \| `"conservative"` \| `"conservative-feat"`) | `"off"` | Pre-1.0 severity-downgrade policy: `conservative` downgrades an inferred Major to Minor; `conservative-feat` also downgrades Minor to Patch |

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[package]]
match = "cargo/callisto-cli"
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
tag-template = "callisto@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["callisto-cli@{version}"]
```

## `[[fixed-group]]` and `[[linked-group]]`

Neither has a config-level default for its fields — both are required when the block is present.

| Key | Type | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | Group identifier, unique across both fixed and linked groups |
| `members` | array of strings | yes, non-empty | Package names in the group |

`[[fixed-group]]`: all members bump in lock-step from the group's alignment base. `[[linked-group]]`: every member receives the highest severity and aligns to the highest target version produced by the members' bumps. Both currently require compatible version grammars; neither is an automatic cross-language version converter.

Example (this repo's own `callisto.toml`):
```toml
[[fixed-group]]
name = "workspace"
members = ["callisto-model", "callisto-manifests", "callisto-graph", "callisto-cli"]
```

## `[init]`

Deprecated. `ecosystems` (array of strings) is parsed so older config files still load, but nothing reads it.

PR #272 (E317) is open and ready for review, and #271 is green and ready to merge. #272's hosted CI is still running.

**#272: a package in `callisto.toml` without its ecosystem is now E317**
- **What changed:** a bare package name is rejected with the `eco/name` form shown. The same applies to `[[package]]` and `[[package-set]]` `match`, and to `product-package` and `[[release.artifact]] package`.
- **Exceptions:** the native name of a platform package stays valid in a group. Changeset entries and `pre.json` keys keep native names.
- **This repo:** its own `callisto.toml` is converted. The specs, `docs/config.md`, `docs/errors.md` (E317, 242 codes) and the identity note are updated.
- **Tests:** fixtures use the qualified form, and new tests cover each rejected position and the CLI path. I removed the tests that could only write a bare rule, since a loaded config can no longer contain one. The two group tests about one package under two spellings now use a dual Cargo and npm package.
- **Verified:** `just ci` passes locally (the log's `exit=0`, coverage 92.71%). The commit is signed and the PR is not a draft.
- **Breaking:** it needs a minor bump on the CLI. A user's existing bare group members will fail until they add the prefix.
- **Cleanup caught:** my scripted conversion altered two unrelated comments (`cargo/npm/twine` in `runner.rs` and one in the init tests). I restored them before committing.

**Left for the next slice (T06 PR 4):** the PR body records this on purpose. With bare rules gone, three things are unreachable but still in the code:
- The second bare pass in `resolve_package_config`.
- `ResolvedConfig::promoted_siblings`.
- The emission of the `bare-rule-matches-multiple-ecosystems` diagnostic.

I held back because removing that diagnostic touches a code that appears in reports, so it goes with the rule-matching-through-the-identity-index change. That slice also removes the dead `from_groups`, `resolve_unique` and `resolve_human`.

Next I'll watch #272's CI, then start T06 PR 4. Tell me if you'd rather I do the scheduled-`cargo deny`-style hygiene items first.

def cut(path, start_marker, end_marker, keep_end=True):
    """Remove text from start_marker up to (not including) end_marker."""
    s = read(path)
    a = s.index(start_marker)
    b = s.index(end_marker, a)

        let pkg_override = resolve_package_config(&id, &package_ecosystems, cfg)?;''', '''        // The first [[package]] rule, in declaration order, whose ecosystem this package has and whose name matches.

import re

p = 'crates/callisto-cli/tests/cli_tests.rs'
s = open(p).read()

mapping = {
    'napi-mod': 'npm/napi-mod',
    'maturin-mod': 'pypi/maturin-mod',
    'tool': 'cargo/tool',
    'npm-only': 'npm/npm-only',
    'py-only': 'pypi/py-only',
    'dual-pkg': 'npm/dual-pkg',
    'pkg-a': 'npm/pkg-a',
    'pkg-b': 'npm/pkg-b',
    'mixed-mod': 'npm/mixed-mod',
    'clean-mod': 'npm/clean-mod',
    'alpha': 'npm/alpha',
    'zeta': 'cargo/zeta',
    '@scope/napi': 'npm/@scope/napi',
}
for old, new in mapping.items():
    s = s.replace('["platformTargets"]["%s"]' % old, '["platformTargets"]["%s"]' % new)
    s = s.replace('["runtimeVersions"]["%s"]' % old, '["runtimeVersions"]["%s"]' % new)
    s = s.replace('["platformTargets"].get("%s")' % old, '["platformTargets"].get("%s")' % new)
    s = s.replace('["runtimeVersions"].get("%s")' % old, '["runtimeVersions"].get("%s")' % new)

s = s.replace('"schemaVersion": 1,', '"schemaVersion": 2,', 1)
open(p, 'w').write(s)

## D01-B: canonical references and the legacy boundary

State today (reproduced and source):

| Surface | Accepts | Emits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release wire (decision, intent, snapshot, manifest, receipt) | `ecosystem/native-name` only | same |
| `release --package` | qualified only; bare gives E227; colon accepted as an alias | n/a |
| `product-package`, `[[release.artifact]] package` | qualified only; bare gives E197 | n/a |
| Changesets, `callisto add`, config groups and rules, `pre.json`, `matrix --package` | bare, `eco:name`, `eco/name` (prefix case-insensitive) | bare when unpromoted, slash when promoted |
| `status`, `version`, `matrix` output | n/a | bare when unpromoted, slash when promoted |
| `callisto init` | n/a | always slash |

Colon is emitted nowhere. The real trap is promotion: a changeset `foo: minor` works until an unrelated `npm/foo` appears, then `status` reports an ambiguous-package error (reproduced; WS-ID-06). It fails loudly, not silently.

Findings that change the scope:
- A changeset entry names an owner package, not a distribution. In a dual Cargo+npm directory `x-core`, `cargo/x-core`, `npm/@x/core` and `@x/core` all write `x-core: minor`, and an entry naming both merges into one bump (reproduced). "The canonical reference" for an entry has no single answer.
- Python selectors use the declared name (`pypi/Foo_Bar`); `foo-bar` and `pypi/foo-bar` give E102. PEP 503 normalization applies only to dependency-name lookup. Canonical-only must choose declared or normalized.
- ADR 1 promises one-commit adoption and rollback with `@changesets/cli`. Canonical `npm/@scope/x` in `.changeset/*.md` and `pre.json` breaks that for npm users. `pre.json` is also changesets-compatible.
- This repo dogfoods the bare forms: `callisto.toml` groups, all 8 `.changeset/*.md`, `AGENTS.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md` (`--package callisto-cli:<bump>`), and 111 bare tags.
- Blast radius if readers become strict: 166 colon literals in about 25 test files (mechanical), 192 bare `PackageId::parse` calls (mostly unit tests), roughly 26 bare `--package` args in CLI tests, and 24 of 236 spec criteria. T06 lists only 11 of them; WS-ID-07, WS-CFG-03/04/08, VER-PRE-01 and WS-ID-10 are missing.
- There is no `migrate` or `doctor` command and no config schema version (`RawConfig` is `deny_unknown_fields`). Only Nx (`nx migrate`) and Lerna (`lerna repair`) ship one among the tools checked (web, from search summaries; not verified on the primary pages).

Options for the legacy-read boundary:

| | Readers | Writers | Cost | Cost to users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 hard break | canonical only | canonical | Large: strict readers, 400+ fixtures, ~24 criteria | Every existing repo, this one included, fails on upgrade and users hand-edit. Breaks ADR 1 rollback |
| M2 warn, then canonical on write | legacy accepted with a warning | canonical | Medium: warning plumbing, a diagnostic code, format-preserving rewrites | Smooth; two spellings persist until a deadline |
| M3 explicit `callisto migrate` | strict after migration; old repos error with a pointer | canonical | Largest: new command, spec, tests, plus strict readers | Auditable one-command rewrite; adoption cost |
| M4 only change writers | unchanged | canonical | Smallest | None; leaves the promotion trap and contradicts "reject new bare aliases" |
| M5 split by surface | canonical required in config, groups, rules, reports, matrix keys, CLI args; changesets and `pre.json` keep native names and resolve at read time | canonical where unambiguous | Medium | Keeps ADR 1 interop; the promotion trap remains only in changesets, where it is loud |

Lean: M5, with colon rejected everywhere (never emitted, so nothing breaks) and an error that names the slash form. It keeps the owner's intent where identity matters (config, reports, CLI), respects ADR 1, and avoids a new command. If you want the owner text taken literally for every authored file, M3 is the only option with an auditable boundary and it should be scheduled as its own PR. Owner qu

pat = re.compile(r'("--package",\s*)"([^"/:\\{}]+):(none|patch|minor|major)"')

    for f in fs:
        if not f.endswith('.rs'):
            continue
        p = os.path.join(d, f)
        s = open(p).read()
        n = pat.sub(lambda m: '%s"cargo/%s:%s"' % (m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)), s)
        if n != s:
            open(p, 'w').write(n)
            changed.append(p)
print('\n'.join(changed))

set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent"
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$GITHUB_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json \
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
      - name: Build the matrix from napi targets and artifact slots
        id: matrix
        if: steps.decision.outputs.release == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent="$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          report="$RUNNER_TEMP/matrix.json"
          # Only packages in the release intent: an unrelated addon adds no build and cannot fail the plan.
          {
            while IFS= read -r package; do
              callisto --format json matrix --package "$package"
            done < <(jq -r '[.operations[].id.package] | unique[]' "$intent")
          } | jq -s '{platformTargets: (map(.platformTargets) | add // {})}' > "$report"
          napi=$(jq -c '[.platformTargets[] | select(.kind=="napi") | .targets[] | {kind: "napi"} + .]' "$report")
          slots=$(jq -c --slurpfile report "$report" '[.artifactSlots[] as $slot
            | ([$report[0].platformTargets[] | select(.kind=="cargo") | .targets[]
                | select(.artifactName == $slot.assetName and .triple == $slot.platform)] | first
              // error("callisto matrix has no entry for artifact slot \($slot.assetName)"))
            | {kind: "cargo"} + .]' "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          {
            echo "matrix=$(jq -cn --argjson napi "$napi" --argjson slots "$slots" '$napi + $slots')"
        with:
          name: napi-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/*.node
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Build and archive the release artifact
        if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo_bin=cargo
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then cargo_bin=cross; fi
          cd "${PACKAGE_DIR:-.}"
          "$cargo_bin" build --release --locked --target "$TRIPLE" --package "$PACKAGE"
          metadata=$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1)

# Lint only projects affected by changes since the base branch. Uses moon's
# project graph to find affected crates, then lints them in one cargo
# invocation (not moon's per-project fan-out) to avoid Cargo's build-lock
# serialization while still skipping unaffected crates entirely.
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then
        echo "No projects affected — skipping lint."
        exit 0
    fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings

import re
import subprocess

names = ['GitHubAttestationPolicyV1Wire', 'PlatformPackageV1Wire', 'RegistryBindingIdWire', 'ReleaseDecisionEntryWire',
         'ReleaseIntentV1Wire', 'ReleaseOperationRoleWire', 'ReleasePrConfigWireV1', 'ReleasePrDecisionWireV2',
         'ReleasePrSnapshotWireV2']
out = subprocess.run(['rg', '-l', r'(struct|enum) (%s)\b' % '|'.join(names), 'crates/callisto-model/src'],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()
for path in out:
    s = open(path).read()
    for name in names:
        m = re.search(r'((?:#\[[^\n]*\]\n)*?)((?:pub(?:\([a-z]+\))? )?(?:struct|enum) %s\b)' % name, s)
        if not m:
            continue
        block = m.group(1)
        d = re.search(r'#\[derive\(([^\]]*)\)\]', block)
        if d and 'JsonSchema' not in d.group(1):
            new_block = block.replace(d.group(0), '#[derive(%s, JsonSchema)]' % d.group(1))
            s = s[:m.start(1)] + new_block + s[m.end(1):]
            print(path, name)
        elif not d:
            print('NO DERIVE', path, name)
    if 'use schemars::JsonSchema' not in s and 'schemars::JsonSchema' not in s.split('#[derive')[0]:
        print('CHECK IMPORT', path)
    open(path, 'w').write(s)

content.text:
PR #286 migrates schemars to 1.x. It's open, signed and not a draft, and `just ci` passes locally. Hosted CI has just started.

- **Code changes:** the `JsonSchema` signatures moved to the 1.x API. Nine wire types (the ones read through `try_from`) now derive `JsonSchema`, because schemars 1 takes the schema from the wire type.
- **User-visible change:** `callisto schema` now prints JSON Schema draft 2020-12. Definitions sit under `$defs` instead of `definitions`, and a fixed string variant is a `const` instead of a one-element `enum`. What the schemas accept is unchanged. The guard tests that validate sample reports against the schemas, and reject mutated ones, pass with only their keys updated. There is a changeset.
- **#275:** this was the only reason it failed to build. Once #286 merges, Dependabot should rebase it and it should go green. Tell me if it doesn't.
- **Sandbox:** this session's sandbox blocked three things: downloading new crates into `~/.cargo/registry`, tests that need network and tool caches (the two `uv lock` tests), and signing commits with your GPG key. I ran only those steps outside it. The commit is verified signed. You can widen the sandbox with `/sandbox` to avoid this next time.

No good reason. I branched each PR off `main` so they could be reviewed and CI'd independently, and I only checked for overlap against what existed at the time. Last time you asked, only #266 and #267 conflicted, so I stacked those two. This time I didn't re-check.

I just tested every pair of open branches for merge conflicts. Seven pairs conflict:

| Conflict | Where |
| --- | --- |
| #274, #276 and #281 against each other | `docs/errors.md`: each adds an error row and bumps the same total-codes count |
| #279 and #280 | `status.rs` |
| #283 (edition 2024) with #274, #278 and #286 (schemars) | `version.rs`, `identity.rs`, and three schema files |

The `errors.md` ones are one-line fixes. The edition PR is the real outlier, since it touches 35 files.

What I'd do:
- **Stack #279 under #280.** They really edit the same function.
- **Merge #283 (edition) last.** I rebase it after the others land, so it has nothing to conflict with.
- **Leave the rest independent, and merge them in this order:** #274, #276, #277, #278, #279/#280, #281, #285, #286. Each merge leaves the next branch to rebase for the `errors.md` count, and I'll do that when you tell me.

A native stack of all of them would force one merge order and make every PR wait on the one below it. These are mostly independent, so I'd avoid that.

Create stacked PRs with `gh stack` (e.g. `gh stack link --base main b1 b2 ...`, or `gh stack link <stack#> <branch>` to grow). GitHub runs CI for every PR in a native stack; plain PRs whose base is another branch get no CI.

---
name: feedback-check-pr-overlap-before-parallel-branches
description: Before opening many PRs off main in parallel, run a pairwise merge-tree conflict check and stack the overlapping ones; the owner noticed the conflicts first
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-21 I opened about a dozen PRs off `main` for independent CI and review, never re-checked overlap, and the owner found the merge conflicts before I did (docs/errors.md count line in three PRs, status.rs in two, the edition PR in five).

**Why:** independent branches look cheap, but every PR that edits a shared line (the errors.md "N numeric codes" count, report builders, a repo-wide refactor like an edition move) conflicts after the first merge, and the owner pays the rebase cost.

**How to apply:** after opening a batch, test every pair with `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only origin/a origin/b` (a loop script is fine). Stack the pairs that really edit the same code with `gh stack link --base main <n1> <n2>` (see [[feedback-use-gh-stack]]). Hold repo-wide mechanical changes (edition, formatting, let-chain collapses) until the others merge, then regenerate them. Give the owner a merge order. After each merge, rebase the next branch for the errors.md count before they ask.

print(ids)

m = re.search(r'(    \{\n      "id": "%s",.*?\n    \},\n)' % re.escape(last), s, re.S)

crit = '''    {

''' % new_id

The tag then pointed at code the registry never received.

A local \`callisto release\` now finds the commit that set each package's release version (the newest commit whose manifest holds the version while its parent's does not) and checks whether the package has commits after it. Only if it does, and the registry already holds the version, it refuses with E320 before any effect, naming the version commit and the fix: check that commit out and run \`callisto release\` again. Verified the same way: from the version commit the rerun adopts the published version (no second publish) and tags that commit.

It never refuses without evidence: a package untouched since its version commit, a version the registry does not hold, an inherited or unreadable version, or a preview with no \`origin\` to observe all proceed as before. Nothing is observed unless a package moved, so ordinary releases make no extra registry calls.

Not changed: the managed route, which already releases the exact merge commit, and a package the previous run tagged on HEAD, which still resumes.

Tests: three unit tests for finding the version commit (untouched, later commit, commit in another package) and an end-to-end test over the fake publishers that checks the refusal has no effects and that the recovery from the version commit tags it without publishing again. The release spec and \`docs/errors.md\` (E320) are updated.

p = 'crates/callisto-model/src/release/digest.rs'
s = open(p).read()


def rep(old, new):
    global s
    assert old in s, old[:60]
    s = s.replace(old, new, 1)


rep('let rendered = format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(bytes.as_ref()));', 'let rendered = lower_hex(Sha256::digest(bytes.as_ref()));')
rep('Ok((Self(format!("{:x}", hasher.finalize())), length))', 'Ok((Self(lower_hex(hasher.finalize())), length))')
# helper before the first macro/definition: append near top after imports
marker = '\n\n'
idx = s.index('macro_rules!')
helper = '''/// Lowercase hexadecimal text of `bytes`; digest outputs do not implement `LowerHex` in every `sha2` release.
fn lower_hex(bytes: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> String {
    use std::fmt::Write;
    bytes.as_ref().iter().fold(String::new(), |mut out, byte| {
        write!(out, "{byte:02x}").expect("writing to a String cannot fail");
        out
    })
}

'''
# place before the line that starts the macro (including preceding doc comments is fine to leave)
line_start = s.rfind('\n', 0, idx) + 1
# walk back over preceding comment/attribute lines
lines = s[:line_start].split('\n')
k = len(lines) - 1
while k > 0 and lines[k - 1].lstrip().startswith(('//', '#[')):
    k -= 1
insert_at = sum(len(l) + 1 for l in lines[:k])
s = s[:insert_at] + helper + s[insert_at:]
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print('ok')

The group includes major releases of \`sha2\` 0.11, \`comfy-table\` 8, \`toml\` 1, \`thiserror\` 2, \`toml_edit\` 0.25, \`petgraph\` 0.8, \`base64\` 0.23, \`rstest\`, \`serial_test\` and \`yaml-rust2\`. Three needed code changes; the rest compiled and passed unchanged.

- \`sha2\`: digest output no longer implements \`LowerHex\`, so a small \`lower_hex\` helper renders the digests (two test sites use an inline equivalent).
- \`comfy-table\`: \`load_preset\` became \`load_style\`. Its default truncation indicator is now an ellipsis instead of three dots, which only shows in a truncated cell.
- \`toml\` 1: \`str::parse::<Value>()\` now parses a single value, not a document. The pyproject reader in \`matrix\` used it, so every \`matrix\` run on a Python package failed with E012 until it parsed the document with \`from_str\`. This is the one with user impact if missed; the existing \`matrix\` tests caught it.

Verified: \`just ci\` passes locally on the updated dependencies." 2>&1 | tail -1

PR #293 fixes the failing Release workflow, and all its CI checks pass, including Test Suite on Ubuntu where the registry tools run. I haven't seen the Release workflow's verify job itself run with the fix. That job is the one that was failing, and it only runs on pushes to main and release dispatches, so merge #293 and re-run it to confirm.

The verify job failed on every push to main since the real-registry e2e tests started failing under CI when Verdaccio, pypiserver or `cargo-http-registry` are missing. That job never installed those tools, and the failure was blocking the 0.12.0 release PR (#248).

#293 moves the three install steps into a local action, `.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools`. The CI test job and the release verify job both use it. Release policy is unchanged: no GitHub Environment, and only `execute` gets registry secrets. `just workflow-contracts`, `just zizmor` and the action-pin check pass locally. The commit is signed and has no session link.

Open PRs waiting on you:

| PR | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| #293 | Release verify job fix (above). Merge this first. |
| #290 | Fix for a release left behind after a later commit. |
| #291 | The E176 error now shows the operation in readable form. |
| #292 | Dependency group update (`sha2`, `comfy-table`, `toml`). Should make Dependabot close #289. |
| #248 | Release PR for 0.12.0. Merge it after #293 and a green Release run. |

None of these overlap, so merge order beyond #293 first doesn't matter.

Still open for v1:
- Warn when the registry's repository metadata doesn't match `origin`.
- Floating `v1` action tag with immutable versions.
- Intel mac and aarch64-linux binaries (this one touches release policy).
- The scratch-registry check, which needs your credentials.
- Your calls: accept ADR 12 and cut 0.12.0.

Found something really concerning about the NPM package release:

1. The release workflow can't finish a multi-package npm publish in one pass. After each npm publish, Callisto checks that the registry lists the new version. It waits only about 14 seconds (4 checks at 2, 4 and 8 seconds), and npm often takes minutes. When the check times out, Callisto stops with E157, even though the publish succeeded. Its documented recovery is "Re-run failed jobs", which picks up where it left off, one package per re-run. The same thing happened on 0.3.1, and I got it through then with repeated manual re-runs. With seven npm packages this time, the release was always going to stop and restart several times.

We need to dig much further into NPM package releases, how long it takes and what do we do here? NPM is not as strict about dependency packages existing before publish right so we could just fire away and check at the end, re-doing anything that had issues? We also should consider longer timeouts and dependent on the reason too right?

Think very thoroughly through this. Timeout might need to be configurable but a sane default needs to work
